findings.screen: Admin console (shell) → CRM sync · Notifications · Audit log
findings.title: All three sections are unreachable for 9 of the 11 role prototypes — the repo gates the whole Admin console to admin/superuser
findings.proto: Every one of the 11 live prototypes ships an Admin console containing these three sections, not just the admin/superuser ones. AISJ_IC_Jury_V4/admin/_scripts.js:2 and AISJ_VC_Analyst_V1/admin/_scripts.js:20 both read `var secs=['fw','wt','rb','qb','tm','crm','bl','pc','nt','al','uc','br']` — the 12-section non-admin console, which still includes crm, nt and al. I ran cmp across all 11: admin/s-crm.html is byte-identical in every prototype including Jury, PA, Analyst and Associate; s-nt.html and s-al.html are identical within each edition and differ across editions only in seeded actor names and 'IC member' vs 'Jury member submitted scores'. The brief's assumption that the non-admin consoles are a read-only variant does NOT hold for these three sections — the jury console carries the same live Connect/Disconnect buttons, the same 10 writable toggles and the same full audit trail. s-nt.html's subtitle scopes it per person: 'Control which platform events trigger email and in-app alerts for your account.'
findings.repo: src/shared/nav.ts — `{ id: "admin", label: "Admin console", icon: "Building2", section: "Settings", roles: ["admin"] }`. Only admin (plus the superuser bypass documented in the file header) reaches /app/admin; program_manager, program_associate and jury in the incubator, and partner, ic_member, associate and analyst in the VC, get no Admin console item at all. src/client/routes/AdminConsolePage.tsx has no section routing to gate in the first place.
findings.gap: Even after CRM sync, Notifications and Audit log are built, 9 of the 11 role prototypes still cannot reach any of them. This is load-bearing for Notifications specifically: the prototype scopes it to 'your account', so a jury member must be able to turn off their own 'New pitchdeck submitted' mail, and today there is no screen they can reach to do it. Two decisions are needed and neither is recorded anywhere in docs/: (a) whether every role really gets a console entry, and (b) whether the non-admin console is read-only — the prototype markup says it is NOT, which is a plausible prototype oversight for CRM credentials and billing but is clearly intentional for Notifications.
findings.fix: Split the console into per-section role lists rather than one nav item: keep tm/crm/bl/pc/su*/uc admin-only, and open nt (per-user, all roles) and al (read-only, all roles) to every internal role. Confirm the read-only question with the client before shipping — flag that giving jury the prototype's live CRM credentials and Credits & billing screens is almost certainly not intended.

findings.screen: Admin console › Evaluation › Question bank (s-qb) → founder clarification round-trip
findings.title: No per-question Q&A model — questions and founder answers are each a single text blob, so bank questions could never be tracked, answered or reported individually
findings.proto: admin/s-qb.html models every question as its own addressable row: 68 `.q-row` elements, each with a `.q-num` ordinal (Q1..Qn) and its own `.q-edit` control, grouped under 13 `.qb-area` accordions with a per-area '<n> questions' count. Both written specs make the round trip per-question: live/specs/incubator.html suggested schema 'founder_clarifications ( id, deck_id ⟶ decks, asked_by ⟶ users, question text, answer text, answered_at )' and cross-cutting behaviour 'Founder clarification portal: founders can respond to evaluator questions (round-trip Q&A tied to a deck)'; live/specs/vc.html carries the identical rows.
findings.repo:
migrations/0001_init.sql:122-131 — queries(id, deck_id, questions TEXT, email_status, founder_response TEXT, created_at, resolved_at): one blob out, one blob back, no asked_by, no per-question answer, no answered_at. src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:495-499 stores the whole letter in `questions`. src/client/routes/FounderPortal.tsx:144-165 renders query.questions as one

and offers a single textarea posting respondQuery(query.id, response). Repo-wide grep for founder_clarifications / answered_at returns 0 hits.
findings.gap: Distinct from the auditor's claim 9 (which is about where question TEXT comes from): even with a bank wired up, there is nowhere to record which bank question was asked on a deck, who asked it, whether the founder answered that specific question, or when — so 'which areas did the founder actually address' can never be computed, and the Query screen's resolution state stays all-or-nothing per letter. The spec chapter that specifies this schema was not cited anywhere in the ten findings.
findings.fix: Introduce query_questions(id, query_id, bank_question_id NULL, area_parameter_id, ordinal, question, answer, answered_at) keyed off the existing queries row; render one answer field per question in FounderPortal and roll answered/unanswered up to the Query screen.

findings.screen: Admin console › Evaluation › Question bank (s-qb), cross-checked against Scoring framework (s-fw)
findings.title: Clarification questions are never auto-triggered — the entire 'send automatically when the AI detects weak signal' mechanism the question bank exists to feed has no implementation
findings.proto: admin/s-qb.html sec-sub: 'These questions are auto-triggered to the startup when the AI detects weak, missing, or contradictory signal in a given area.' admin/s-fw.html 'AI engine behaviour' card, second tog-row: 'Auto-trigger clarification questions' / 'Send targeted questions to startup when AI detects weak signal', shipped with class `tog on` (default ON). Byte-identical in all 11 role consoles.
findings.repo: The only code path that creates a query is the manual pipeline.post('/decks/:id/queries', requireRole(...)) at src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:487-499, which returns 400 questions_required unless a human supplies free text, and is reached only from QueryPage's Send button. `INSERT INTO queries` appears nowhere in src/ except that handler (migrations/0005_seed_founder_decks.sql:11 and 0020_seed_demo_refresh.sql:653 are demo seeds). src/server/ai/evaluate.ts and src/server/queue.ts never touch the queries table after scoring. src/server/scheduled.ts exports only runReminders and runStuckSweep (the two cron jobs wired in src/server/index.ts:71-77). org_settings (migrations/0001_init.sql:18-26; its only later ALTER is criteria_version in 0009) has no automation toggle column, and no config route writes one.
findings.gap: The prototype's clarification loop is automatic and admin-switchable; the repo's is 100% manual. Even once a question bank exists, nothing would fire it: there is no trigger on evaluation completion, no toggle to turn it off, and no detection of 'contradictory' signal at all (only weak and missing are derived). This is the mechanism that makes the question bank worth building, and the auditor's ten findings cover the bank's data/UI but never state that the trigger itself is absent.
findings.fix: Add org_settings.auto_query_enabled (default 1) plus the s-fw toggle, and fire query creation from the post-evaluation path in src/server/ai/evaluate.ts / queue.ts when weak or missing areas exist, drawing question text from the new bank; keep the manual Query screen as the override.

findings.screen: Admin console › Evaluation › Rubric anchors (s-rb) ⟷ Question bank trigger (s-qb / s-fw)
findings.title: The 'weak signal' that selects clarification areas is the All-Decks cohort rating threshold, not the rubric's Weak band — moving a cohort threshold silently re-targets founder questions
findings.proto: s-qb sec-sub scopes the trigger to 'weak, missing, or contradictory signal in a given area' — an AREA-level judgement, which s-rb and both specs define only on the BRD five-band scale (live/specs/incubator.html §7: v≥3 → Weak(3), else Insufficient(4); admin/_scripts.js:263 RUBRICS gives each area its own 3–4 and 0–2 descriptors). The cohort thresholds are a deliberately separate concept in the same console: admin/s-fw.html's 'Cohort rating thresholds' block says 'Define the rating bands evaluators see on the All Decks overview' (Best / Mediocre / Poor, #thr-best 7.0, #thr-poor 5.0).
findings.repo: src/server/routes/decks.ts:63-65 derives weak_areas as `... AND s.value < (SELECT o.threshold_mediocre FROM org_settings o WHERE o.edition = d.edition)`. threshold_mediocre is the admin-editable cohort threshold (migrations/0001_init.sql:25; src/shared/scoring.ts:36-40 cohortRating; ConfigPage ThresholdsSection; PUT /api/config/thresholds at src/server/routes/config.ts:312). Those labels flow straight into the founder letter via src/shared/queries.ts:47 and QueryPage.tsx:145. No rubric band value is consulted anywhere in the clarification path.
findings.gap: Two unrelated scales are conflated. scoring.ts:26-40 even documents that the cohort thresholds are 'Distinct from the fixed rubric signal bands above', yet the clarification loop is gated on them: an admin raising 'Poor — below' from 5.0 to 6.5 to re-bucket decks on the All Decks overview also widens which parameters get asked about, and an area scored 5.5 is never queried even though the BRD calls 5–6 Moderate and 3–4 Weak. Fixing the band scale (auditor claim 3) alone does not fix this, because the trigger never reads a band at all.
findings.fix: Once the 5-band scale lands, derive weak_areas from the rubric band (value < 5, i.e. Weak or Insufficient) or from an explicit configurable clarification threshold, and leave threshold_mediocre to cohort rating only.

findings.screen: Admin console › Organisation › Credits & billing (s-bl) + Price configuration (s-pc)
findings.title: Both billing sections are role-universal in the prototype; the repo gives non-admin roles no billing surface whatsoever
findings.proto: s-bl.html and s-pc.html are present in EVERY role console, not just admin/superuser — verified by listing $SPLIT/live-panels/<PROTO>/admin/ for AISJ_IC_Jury_V4, AISJ_IC_PA_V3 and AISJ_VC_Analyst_V1: each carries the 12-section set (al, bl, br, crm, fw, nt, pc, qb, rb, tm, uc, wt) including bl and pc; the admin console adds only the four Sign-up sections. The s-bl file is byte-identical across all 11 prototypes (md5 fb1aaafcc356eb793096391d568913d2), as is the s-pc iframe host (fd8f743deac342625eed103fcd754013). ADMIN-BRIEF.md:42-43 marks both as "all roles" and :54 confirms every non-admin role carries 12 sections.
findings.repo: src/shared/nav.ts:110 { id: "admin", … roles: ["admin"] } and :111 { id: "billing", label: "Buy credits", roles: ["admin"] } (VC twins at :177-178) — the entire console and the only credits screen are admin-only. Server side matches: every config editor is requireRole("admin") (src/server/routes/config.ts:122, 360, 372, 390), and GET /api/config/summary (config.ts:99-114) hands the credits balance to non-admins only as a bare number for the Upload strip. There is no read-only billing view for jury / program_manager / program_associate / partner / ic_member / associate / analyst.
findings.gap: The prototype's gating rule is "everyone sees Credits & billing and Price configuration; only admin/superuser see the Sign-up group", and the brief calls that gating part of the spec. The repo's rule is "only admin sees anything". So six of the seven internal roles lose a surface the prototype grants them, and the read-only variant of these two sections — which is a distinct build (view without the Publish/Buy/Upgrade actions) — has no counterpart. Claims 1 and 2 report the sections as missing for admin but never mention that they are missing for six further roles, which changes both the scope of the build and the permission tests it needs.
findings.fix: Decide the read-only contract first (balance + usage history + plan visible to all internal roles; Buy/Upgrade/Publish admin-only), then open the nav entries with a role-scoped read-only mode rather than duplicating screens.

findings.title: programs.capital_deployed is write-only dead data — the API accepts it and no report ever reads it, and there is no unutilised column at all
findings.proto: AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/admin/s-sufund.html subtitle: 'Record, program-wise, how much of each fund is allotted, deployed, and still unutilised. These figures feed the Capital Deployment & Pacing report.' Table columns Allotted (₹ Cr) | Deployed (₹ Cr) | Unutilised (₹ Cr) | Utilisation. docs/FINISH-PLAN.md §8 records the same ask from the Jul 24 demo: 'For VC programs, capture fund amount / allocated / deployed so Capital Deployment reports show real data.'
findings.repo: programs.capital_deployed is written at src/server/routes/programs.ts:212+224 (create) and :282+297 (update) and echoed at :239/:311 — and never read. `grep -rn "capital_deployed" src/` outside programs.ts hits only src/server/routes/analytics.ts:205, which selects `pf.capital_deployed` from the **portfolio** table (per-deck), a different column; src/server/routes/analytics.ts:220-235 loadFundTotals sums only `fund_size` and `fund_allocated` from programs. migrations/0011_program_hierarchy.sql:23-36 shows programs has fund_size / fund_allocated / capital_deployed and no unutilised column.
findings.gap: Claim 10 credits the repo with 'the API can already take the values' and claim 11 asserts analytics 'consumes capital_deployed'. Both overstate the wiring: the value an admin can set is dropped on the floor, so the figure the prototype says feeds Capital Deployment & Pacing reaches no report at all. Separately, the prototype's three-column model (allotted / deployed / unutilised) cannot be stored — fund_allocated means 'allocated', not 'unutilised' — so claim 11's reconciliation check has no second operand until the schema changes. This turns claim 10 from 'API exists, no screen' into 'API exists, no screen, and the write goes nowhere'.
findings.fix: Decide whether program-level deployment is authored (admin figures) or derived (sum of portfolio.capital_deployed) and wire loadFundTotals to it either way; add the unutilised figure (stored or computed); then build the s-sufund grid with per-row editing, the utilisation bar and the ±0.5 Cr reconciliation line from claim 11.

findings.title: GET /api/activity cannot back an audit log at all — hard cap of 50, no pagination, no date range, no filters, no export
findings.proto: admin/s-al.html sec-sub: 'Full timestamped trail of all configuration changes, score overrides, team actions, and billing events.' The seeded rows span three days and mix clock times, 'Yesterday' and absolute dates ('3 Jun'), so the section is explicitly a historical trail, not a recent-activity peek.
findings.repo: src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:795 — `const limit = Math.min(Math.max(Number(c.req.query("limit") ?? 12) || 12, 1), 50);`. The query at pipeline.ts:817-824 is `ORDER BY e.created_at DESC, e.rowid DESC LIMIT ?` with no OFFSET, no cursor and no date predicate; the only filters are programId and cohortId. The response (pipeline.ts:840-853) returns a bare `events` array with no total and no next cursor. The deck-scoped alternative, GET /decks/:id/events (pipeline.ts:742), is unbounded but per-deck, and its client helper src/client/api.ts:458 getDeckEvents has zero call sites.
findings.gap: Audited item 4 treats this as a placement-and-shape problem ('wrong place and wrong shape'), which implies the fix is to re-render the same endpoint inside the console. It is not: any Audit log section built on /api/activity can never display more than the 50 most recent workspace events, can never be paged back to the '3 Jun' rows the prototype shows, and can never be filtered by category, actor or date or exported. The endpoint needs cursor pagination and a filter surface regardless of how the event model in items 5-9 is fixed, and that work is invisible in the current findings.
findings.fix: Add cursor pagination (created_at + rowid keyset, `next_cursor` in the response), a `from`/`to` date range, and actor/category/action filters to GET /api/activity; keep the 12-row Dashboard rail as a `limit=12` caller so nothing regresses. Add CSV export once categories exist. Size this alongside the schema work in item 5 — the new event table should be designed with the keyset index from the start.

findings.title: Notification preferences are per-USER with a specified default mask — the repo has no per-user settings storage of any kind, so claim 2's org-level framing would build the wrong model
findings.proto: admin/s-nt.html subtitle: '…trigger email and in-app alerts for your account' — per person, not per workspace, and the section ships in all 11 role consoles (see the previous item). The seed also fixes the DEFAULT MASK: 8 of the 10 `.tog` elements carry class `on` and exactly 2 do not — 'Startup responded to clarification questions' and 'New team member accepted invite' — and the VC copy (AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/admin/s-nt.html) uses the identical 8-on/2-off split, so the defaults are deliberate, not incidental.
findings.repo: There is no per-user preference storage anywhere. `users` (migrations/0001_init.sql:5-14, plus every ALTER — 0015_roles_users.sql:19 user_type, 0021_alias_titles_and_tags.sql:10 title) has no preferences column and no side table. The only settings table is `org_settings` (migrations/0001_init.sql:18), a per-EDITION singleton keyed on `edition` — one row for the whole workspace, which cannot express a per-person mask. src/client/routes/AccountPage.tsx has profile fields and the alias title only, with no settings section to hang toggles on. src/server/email/outbox.ts sendEmail has no recipient-preference lookup and no suppression seam.
findings.gap: Claim 2 reports this as an admin/org-level surface ('An admin cannot see or change which events email them'), which would lead to a single org_settings JSON column. The prototype requires a row per (user × event) with a seeded 8-on/2-off default applied to every user at creation (src/server/routes/users.ts) and to all 30-odd seeded demo logins, plus a suppression check inside sendEmail so the 7 existing call sites stay unchanged. That is a materially different and larger build than the reported gap describes, and getting it wrong is expensive to unwind once demo data is seeded.
findings.fix: Add `notification_prefs (user_id, event_key, enabled)` with the 10 event keys, seed the 8-on/2-off default in a migration for existing users and in the create-user path for new ones, expose GET/PUT /api/notifications/prefs, and put the lookup inside sendEmail keyed on toEmail so no call site changes. Note that only 1 of the 10 events has a producer today (audited item 3), so the toggles ship inert for 9 until those producers exist — sequence this after the producers or the section is a dead screen.

findings.title: Roster has no re-role, no rename and no member removal — the API supports two of the three and nothing calls it
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/admin/s-tm.html — the members card header carries an 'Invite member' button, and admin/_scripts.js:119-136 tmRender() ends every row with `.t-acts`: `<button class="t-btn">Edit</button><button class="t-btn del">Remove</button>` for active members and `Resend` / `Cancel` for the pending one (:126-127). 'Delete user' is also one of the grantable tasks in the permissions matrix (admin/_scripts.js:176 `{id:'deleteuser', l:'Delete user'}`), alongside 'Activate user' and 'Deactivate user'. Byte-identical in AISJ_ICAdmin_V6 and both VC admin builds.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/AdminConsolePage.tsx:213-228 renders exactly one row action — Activate/Deactivate — and the only other per-row control is the alias-title input at :170-198. Meanwhile src/server/routes/users.ts:302-348 (PATCH /api/users/:id) already validates and applies `role` (:320-325) and `name` (:317-318), and src/client/api.ts:791-800 exposes both in updateUser(), so the re-role/rename API is live but has no caller. There is no DELETE route for users anywhere: users.ts registers only GET "/" (:173), PATCH "/me" (:196), POST "/" (:222) and PATCH "/:id" (:302), and `grep -rn '\.delete(' src/server/routes/*.ts` finds delete routes only in config.ts and programs.ts.
findings.gap: An admin who mis-assigns a role at creation, or whose staff member changes job, cannot fix it from the console — the only escape is a hand-crafted PATCH. Removing a departed member is absent end-to-end (no API, no UI); deactivation is the only approximation, and it leaves the row and the seat in place. The auditor's claims 7/8/9 cover the pending badge, the permissions matrix and the workspace toggle, but never the roster's own Edit/Remove actions.
findings.fix: Add a role <select> and a Remove control to each manageable row in AdminConsolePage (reusing updateUser for role/name), and add a guarded DELETE /api/users/:id (block self, block superuser, same-edition only) or an explicit soft-delete, mirroring the prototype's Edit / Remove pair.

findings.title: No way to nominate or change the account's Super User — ownership is permanently whatever the seed created
findings.proto: s-tm.html card 4 states the rule that implies the flow exists elsewhere: 'The account owner (Super User) is fixed and can't be overridden here.' The flow itself is _rest.html:1206 `#su-superbox` on the sus-team screen, rendered by _scripts.js:3247-3260 `renderSuper()` in three states — 'You are the super user', 'Super user — {email} · only one super user per account' with a `su-chgbtn` 'Change', and a required nomination form ('Nominate a super user' + email + plan select + 'Set super user', note 'A super user has full platform access… Only one super user is allowed per account'). Handlers `suSetSuper()` :3262-3266 and `suClearSuper()` :3268. tmRoles.inc/inv both list 'Super user' / 'Managing Partner/Super user' as a real role.
findings.repo: src/shared/roles.ts:210-212 `creatableStaffRoles` explicitly filters out 'superuser', so POST /api/users can never create one (validated at src/server/routes/users.ts:239-244 via isCreatableStaffRole). src/server/routes/users.ts:307 rejects any PATCH touching a superuser row with `immutable_superuser` 403, and :311 blocks self-edit — so an existing superuser cannot be demoted and nobody can be promoted. No other route or script assigns role='superuser' (grep "'superuser'" over src/server/ finds only the requireRole bypass at auth/middleware.ts:25 and comparisons). The only superuser rows in the system are the two seeded at migrations/0002_seed.sql:45 and :51.
findings.gap: Account ownership can never be transferred, nominated or recovered. If the seeded superuser leaves the org, the account has no owner and no path to appoint one — the prototype treats nominating exactly one super user as a required, changeable step.
findings.fix: Add an ownership-transfer action (superuser-only) that atomically promotes one active staff user to 'superuser' and demotes the current owner to 'admin', enforcing the one-superuser-per-edition invariant in the DB, plus the 'Super user — {email} · Change' card on the Team & roles screen.

findings.title: Spec §10 grants Program Managers and Client Admins parameter configuration by default; the repo hard-codes it to admin/superuser with no grant path
findings.proto: scratchpad/spec-incubator.html.txt §10 Cross-Cutting Behaviours (the design team's formal spec, which the brief says outranks markup inference): “Permissions: parameter configuration is editable by Super Users, Program Managers and Client Admins by default; other roles are read-only unless granted ‘Configure 3 additional parameters’ in Admin → Team & roles.” The matching task id exists in the console matrix (admin/_scripts.js:174 `{id:'configparams', l:'Configure 3 additional parameters'}`) and permDefaults:190 grants it to 'Prog. manager'. The role sidebars agree: si-coreparams is present in AISJ_IC_PM_V5/_sidebar.html:10, AISJ_IC_PA_V3, AISJ_VC_Partner_V1, AISJ_VC_Associate_V1, AISJ_VC_Analyst_V1 and AISJ_VC_IC_member_V2 (absent only in the IC Jury build).
findings.repo: src/shared/nav.ts:105 (incubator) and :173 (VC) both declare `{ id: "coreparams", … roles: ["admin"] }`, so a PM/PA/partner/associate/analyst never sees the screen and RequireNav blocks the route. src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:32 `const canEdit = user?.role === "admin" || user?.role === "superuser";`. Server-side, src/server/routes/config.ts:151, 215, 261 and 291 all use requireRole("admin"), and src/server/auth/middleware.ts:25 bypasses only `superuser` — program_manager is refused 403.
findings.gap: The single permission default the written spec states explicitly is inverted in the repo: the role the Jul-24 decisions made the decision maker (PM) cannot configure any parameter, on any screen, at any tier — and because the grant surface (Admin → Team & roles task matrix, claim 8) does not exist either, there is no way to restore it. This is the concrete, user-visible consequence of the missing matrix and is not stated in any of the 12 claims. Lane overlap: the fix touches the Core Parameters lane, but the authority to grant it lives in Team & roles.
findings.fix: Give `coreparams` roles ["admin","program_manager"] (and the VC equivalents the spec implies), let MyParamsPage/ConfigPage compute canEdit from that same source, and relax the server guards to requireRole("admin","program_manager") — ideally reading a persisted permission row once the matrix from claim 8 exists, so the default is data rather than another constant.

findings.title: A role/additional parameter can never be given a weight — both specs require raising it to 5% or 10%
findings.proto: Both written specs say it three times each, independently of the prototype markup. incubator §6.2 / vc §6.2: 'Default weight Informational (not weighted into the composite **unless the org (fund) raises it to 5% / 10%**).' §7 Scoring & Aggregation: 'Role-custom parameters default to Informational and are excluded from the composite **unless weighted (5% / 10%)**.' And the suggested schema in §9 types the column as `weight[ Informational | 5% | 10% | numeric for standard ]`.
findings.repo: No path exists to set it. src/server/routes/config.ts:246 inserts every additional param with the weight literal baked into the SQL: `INSERT INTO parameters (…, weight, informational, …) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 1, ?, ?, ?, 1)`. The only weight editor, PUT /api/config/parameters, actively refuses informational rows — config.ts:170 `if (!p || p.informational === 1) return c.json({ error: "invalid_param" }, 400)`. PUT /api/config/additional-params/:id (config.ts:258-286) accepts only `name` and `prompt`. MyParamsPage.tsx renders no weight field. So the value is unreachable from the UI, the API and the admin surface alike.
findings.gap: The spec's stated escalation path — an org promotes one of its 9 role parameters into the weighted composite at 5% or 10% — is not representable. The 0-weight informational status is hard-coded at INSERT and defended by an explicit 400 on the one route that could change it, so this needs a schema-adjacent change plus a UI, not a config edit. (Note the build's counter-invariant, FINISH-PLAN.md:62/184/383, 'composite stays core-13 = 100%', is a deliberate design stance — but it was never reconciled against this spec clause, and no doc mentions the 5%/10% option at all.)
findings.fix: Allow PUT /api/config/parameters (or a dedicated route) to set weight ∈ {0, 5, 10} on informational params, surface it as a select on MyParamsPage next to the name/prompt editors, and decide explicitly whether a promoted param joins the core-13 denominator or forms a documented 100+N total.

findings.title: The nine seeded role parameters do not match the specs' canonical tables in either edition
findings.proto: Both specs give a canonical 3×3 table and the incubator one adds a rule making it binding: 'Consistency rule: **these role-parameter names are canonical across every file.** The Super User / Admin "My Parameters — Role configuration" panel defines them for all roles.' Incubator §6.2 — Program Manager: TRL stage · Product-Market Fit · Traction; Program Associate: Program fit · Investment stage · Ask; Jury Member: Barriers of entry · Scalability · Industry growth. VC §6.2 (JP_ADDL) — Investment Associate: Thesis fit · Investment stage · Ask / Ticket size fit; Partner/Principal: TRL stage · Product-Market Fit · Traction; IC Member: Barriers of entry · Scalability · Exit attractiveness. Each row also carries a specific scorer-facing description and AI extraction prompt.
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql seeds entirely different names and prompts: incubator PA = 'Program & Mandate Fit' / 'Application Readiness' / 'Founder Coachability Signal'; PM = 'Program Fit' / 'Mentor Engagement Potential' / 'Cohort Contribution Potential'; jury = 'Founder Resilience & Coachability' / 'Product-Market Fit Signal' / 'Team Execution Capability'. VC associate = 'Thesis & Mandate Fit' / 'Deal Readiness' / 'Founder Conviction Signal'; partner = 'Ownership & Return Math' / 'Portfolio Construction Fit' / 'Conviction to Sponsor'; ic_member = 'Founder Resilience & Coachability' / 'Product-Market Fit Signal' / 'Team Execution Capability'. Not one of the 18 spec names appears in the repo: grep -rn 'TRL|Barriers of entry|Exit attractiveness|Thesis fit|Investment stage' over src/, migrations/, docs/FINISH-PLAN.md and HANDOFF.md returns zero hits, so no decision to diverge was ever recorded.
findings.gap: The migration's header documents a decision about WHICH ROLES own a set, but silently invented new content for all 9×2 parameters. Since these are the exact parameters each role scores and the AI pre-fills from their prompts (spec §10: 'the 3 role parameters configured in My Parameters are the exact parameters that role scores'), the build evaluates every deck against a different rubric than the specification defines — and 'TRL stage' in particular (a named deliverable in the incubator PM lens) is scored nowhere.
findings.fix: Reconcile the two lists explicitly: either reseed migrations/0013 with the specs' canonical names/descriptions/prompts, or record a decision in FINISH-PLAN §8 that the seeded set supersedes the spec table and why.

The specs outrank inference from markup per ADMIN-BRIEF.md:64, and the seeded prototype tickets are billing ones ("Credit top-up not reflected", "Invoice for Q2 usage").
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:192 gives tickets only `billing_routed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`; migrations/0018_scheduling_issues_ai_health.sql:56-61 adds category/severity/area/assignee_id/resolution/updated_at but no approval state. src/server/routes/support.ts:69 sets the flag by keyword match (body.billing === true || /\b(billing|credit|invoice|payment|refund)\b/i), and POST /:id/status (support.ts:80-90) only toggles open|closed. The UI is a checkbox and a badge: SupportPages.tsx:73-74 "Billing / credits related", :116 <Badge tone="amber">Billing</Badge>. No approver, no states, no transitions.
findings.gap: A ticket that costs money (a credit refund, a top-up dispute, a plan change) is meant to walk an approval chain with a recorded state and an approver; the repo just tags it amber and leaves it open/closed. Every one of the 13 claims is prototype-markup-derived — none looks at the specs' cross-cutting billing requirement, so this whole approval workflow is unreported even though the spec names both the behaviour and the column.
findings.fix: Add billing_approval_state (requested|approved|rejected) plus approver_id/decided_at to tickets, gate the transition to admin/superuser, and surface it in the admin ticket view.

findings.title: No Organization / Fund entity — every billing object the spec anchors on org_id has nothing to hang from; plan and credits are per-EDITION globals
findings.proto: spec-incubator.html.txt:11 lists Organization as a core entity and :136 draws "Organization 1---1 Subscription ---(plan tier) 1---inf CreditLedgerEntry"; §13 anchors all three billing tables on it — subscriptions(… org_id ⟶ organizations …):234, credit_ledger(… org_id ⟶ organizations …):235, support_tickets(… org_id ⟶ organizations …):236 (vc-spec.txt:219-221 uses fund_id ⟶ funds). §14 exposes it as GET /orgs/:id/credits. The prototype sells to organizations throughout: ORG_PLANS 25-seat / 100-seat enterprise SKUs, AET_PLANS seat caps, s-bl's "Enterprise · 5 seats".
findings.repo: No organizations/funds table exists — `grep -c "CREATE TABLE" migrations/*.sql` totals 26 and none is an org. Billing state lives in org_settings, keyed by edition: migrations/0001_init.sql:18-26 (edition PRIMARY KEY, plan, credits_balance), with the file's own header at :1 reading "Single-tenant: one implicit organization". Every credit path is edition-scoped: reserveCredits/refundCredits in src/server/decks/versions.ts:40-55, and config.ts:377/400 "UPDATE org_settings … WHERE edition = ?". HANDOFF.md:621 records the single-tenant choice as deliberate.
findings.gap: Claims 2, 6, 7 and 10 each report a missing billing object (ledger, enterprise tier, org plans, subscriptions) without naming the reason none of them can be built as specified: there is no customer record to attach them to. Credits and plan are shared by every user of an edition, so two customers cannot hold different balances, and 'per-org' anything — subscription, seat allowance, invoice, trial grant — has no key. This is the structural precondition for the whole lane and it is unreported; whoever picks up the billing work needs it stated before they start, together with the decision on whether single-tenant stays.
findings.fix: Decide explicitly whether the product stays single-tenant. If billing is to be built, introduce organizations/funds and re-key org_settings, credit_ledger, subscriptions and tickets onto it; if not, record that the billing SKUs are demo-only and cannot be per-customer.

findings.screen: Credits & billing / Buy credits vs Price configuration (s-pc)
findings.title: The repo's hardcoded credit-pack ladder contradicts the master price table the prototype makes editable
findings.proto: s-pc's "Pay-as-you-go credit packs" table ("One-time purchase · Credits never expire", "Minimum 10 units") defines base rate #base-inr 500/deck and THREE packs: #p10-inr 5000 (₹500/deck, 0%), #p50-inr 20000 (₹400/deck, 20%, "Most popular") and #p100-inr 30000 (₹300/deck, 40%, "Best value"), with USD/GBP/EUR columns (60/47/55, 240/189/221, 360/283/331) and calcPacks() deriving per-deck and saving from the base rate. The account overlay's PACKS (_scripts.js:2809) instead sells 20/35/50-credit packs at ₹10,000/₹15,750/₹20,000 (pro) and ₹12,000/₹19,250/₹25,000 (premium).
findings.repo: src/client/routes/BuyCreditsPage.tsx:20-31 hardcodes only the account-overlay ladder (20/35/50 at ₹500/₹450/₹400 and ₹600/₹550/₹500 per deck). Nothing in the repo carries the 10/50/100-unit ladder, the ₹500 base rate, the ₹300/deck floor or the 40% saving; src/server/routes/config.ts:394-395 merely bounds a purchase at 1..1000 credits.
findings.gap: Two prototype sources state different SKUs, and s-pc is explicitly the master ("changes here update the public pricing page and all in-app plan displays"). The repo happens to match the overlay, so a Price-configuration build seeded from s-pc would immediately disagree with the shipped Buy-credits screen — different pack sizes, a different top pack (100 vs 50), and a per-deck floor of ₹300 vs ₹400. Claims 1, 9 and 13 all touch these screens and none flags the conflict, so the finish work would silently pick one and break the other.
findings.fix: Get the client to rule on which ladder is canonical, then drive Buy credits from the stored price table instead of the literal in BuyCreditsPage.tsx.

findings.screen: Legal DD / Investment DD (VC) — second consumer of Required documents
findings.title: The VC diligence document sets (per-item not_requested → awaiting → submitted → verified, with Verify all) are absent — both DD stages are a single free-text notes row
findings.proto: specs/vc.html §8.3 step 2: 'Diligence — legal DD and investment DD document sets, each item not_requested → awaiting → submitted → verified (with a "Verify all" bulk action)'; §Key enums line 127: 'Document/diligence status: not_requested → awaiting → submitted → verified'; §3 line 166 assigns 'required documents' configuration to the VC Admin. The admin section that seeds these items is AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/admin/s-sudocs.html (scoped by Fund, six toggles including 'Audited financials · Last 2 years'), and the bulk action is implemented at AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:2750 / suVerifyAll:2754.
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:144-150 `investment_dd (id, deck_id, notes, mp_approved, created_at)` and :171-176 `legal_dd (id, deck_id, notes, created_at)` — one free-text notes row per deck, no items and no status. src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx `investmentdd` and `legaldd` stage configs render columns ["startup","sector","ai","avg","status"] only — no document rows, no per-item status, no Verify all. migrations/0020_seed_demo_refresh.sql:692 puts the entire legal-DD checklist into one prose sentence ('Checklist with external counsel: cap table, IP assignment, key customer contracts, employment agreements. Status tracked here; the work itself happens off-platform.').
findings.gap: Claim 3 measures document readiness only on the incubator side (deck_onboarding.documents_status) and concludes 'a single roll-up field'. On the VC side there is not even a roll-up: the required-documents checklist has a second, entirely unreported consumer — the two DD stages — where the spec asks for per-item rows with the same four-state lifecycle plus a bulk verify. The seeded prose comment shows the intent was explicitly deferred off-platform, which the audit should record.
findings.fix: Model DD items as rows (deck_id, set ∈ legal|investment, name, status, file_url, verified_by) seeded from the per-fund checklist, surface them in a DD drawer on the legaldd / investmentdd screens, and add the Verify all bulk action — sharing the same table as the incubator's signup_documents so one document model serves both editions.

findings.title: Enterprise annual unit tiers (100–500 units/year) are absent — no annual plan concept exists
findings.proto: Price-config "Enterprise annual plans" card, badge "Annual contract · Units reset yearly", sub "Annual invoice. Role-based 3-parameter system. Dedicated account manager. Unlimited evaluators." Rows #e100/#e200/#e300/#e400/#e500-inr = 60000/110000/150000/180000/200000 with USD 720/1319/1799/2159/2399, GBP 566/1038/1416/1699/1888, EUR 661/1212/1653/1983/2204; computed per-deck ₹600/550/500/450/400 and saving —/8%/17%/25%/33% via calcEnt() (basePerDeck=600); "500 units" carries a "Best value" badge; footer "Enterprise invoiced annually in INR. International billing available via wire transfer. GST invoice provided."
findings.repo: NONE. src/shared/plans.ts:8 defines only standard|pro|premium; migrations/0001_init.sql:20 constrains `plan IN ('standard','pro','premium')`. No `renews_at`, no annual/one-time distinction, no unit allowance.
findings.gap: No enterprise tier, no annual contract, no yearly unit reset, no per-deck effective-rate maths.
findings.fix: Model plan tiers as data rows (name, billing_period, unit allowance, price per currency, active flag, badge) rather than a hardcoded enum; add subscriptions(status, renews_at) per the written spec; implement the annual unit reset.

findings.title: Individual monthly subscriptions (Standard ₹999/mo, Pro ₹1,999/mo) and the billing-cycle concept are absent
findings.proto: Price-config "Individual plans" card, badge "Monthly subscription · Per seat", sub "Individual subscriptions billed monthly. Upgrade or downgrade anytime." #ind-table rows: Standard #std-inr 999 / #std-usd 12 / #std-gbp 9 / #std-eur 11, badge "No configurable params", desc "20 decks/mo · All 13 areas · Override & remark"; Pro #pro-inr 1999 / $24 / £19 / €22, badge "3 configurable params", desc "Unlimited decks · CRM sync · Intro call prompts"; both with an Active toggle. Success screen renders cycle strings "Monthly · renews 4 Jul 2026" / "Annual subscription · renews yearly" / "Fixed pack · one-time purchase" / "Pay-as-you-go · credits never expire" (_scripts.js:3044-3052).
findings.repo: NONE. No subscription table (`grep "CREATE TABLE" migrations/*.sql`), no renewal date, no monthly deck quota, no upgrade/downgrade path. The written spec explicitly asks for `subscriptions(org_id, plan, status, renews_at)` — live/specs/incubator.html §13.
findings.gap: Three of the four billing cycles the prototype depicts (monthly, annual, one-time) have no representation; only an unbounded credit balance exists.
findings.fix: Add the `subscriptions` table from the written spec with a billing_period and renews_at; render the correct cycle string per purchase; implement the monthly quota for the Standard subscription.

findings.title: Free-trial configuration (deck limit, expiry, pricing-page visibility) is hardcoded, not configurable
findings.proto: Price-config "Free trial" card, badge "Always free · No card required", tag "₹0 always", head "Free trial — 3 deck evaluations / Included with every new account. Full AI evaluation across all 13 areas." Rows: "Free deck limit" number 3 ("Applies to all plans at signup"), "Free trial expiry" number 0 ("Days before free trial expires (0 = never)"), "Show free trial on pricing page" toggle on ("Displayed as first option"). Also .ac-trialstrip "Free trial — 3 decks included" with Deck 1/2/3 chips (_rest.html #ac-payg).
findings.repo: migrations/0002_seed.sql:11-13 seeds credits_balance 3, then migrations/0007_config_plans_credits.sql:12 overwrites it with 50 for demo purposes. No trial entity, no grant-on-signup path, no expiry, no trial flag.
findings.gap: The free trial is a one-off seed value, not a product rule: a new org gets nothing automatically, the limit cannot be changed, and expiry does not exist.
findings.fix: Store trial_deck_limit / trial_expiry_days / show_on_pricing_page in the pricing config; grant trial credits with reason 'trial_grant' on org creation; honour expiry (0 = never).

findings.title: s-pc is a PLATFORM-OWNER console, not a tenant screen — its sibling sections and the platform-owner role above org admin are all absent and unreported
findings.proto: The decoded document renders its own full chrome, not a section body: .sb-ctx "Super admin · Price configuration"; sidebar group .sb-lbl "Platform settings" with four items — Dashboard (ti-layout-dashboard), Price configuration (ti-coin, .on), "Billing & invoices" (ti-receipt), "Currency & FX" (ti-world); a second group "Evaluation" (Scoring framework, Team & roles, Audit log); and .sb-foot avatar "SA" over .sb-un "Super admin" / .sb-ur "Platform owner". The topbar actions are "Preview pricing page" and "Publish changes", and the body says these prices "update the public pricing page and all in-app plan displays" — i.e. the vendor's master SKU table, not one customer's settings.
findings.repo: src/shared/roles.ts:9-25 defines only tenant roles (INCUBATOR_ROLES superuser/admin/program_manager/program_associate/jury/founder; VC_ROLES superuser/admin/partner/ic_member/associate/analyst) — "superuser" is the Managing Partner / org owner, not a platform operator. No platform surface exists: a whole-repo grep (excluding node_modules/dist) for priceconfig|price_config|pricing|currency|invoice|credit_ledger|subscription returns only src/server/routes/support.ts:69. migrations/0001_init.sql:1 states the design: "Single-tenant: one implicit organization".
findings.gap: Claim 1 treats s-pc as one more admin-console section, which would put the vendor's master price list, FX rates and GST registration inside the customer's own admin. The prototype places it behind a distinct "Platform owner" identity with three further platform sections — Dashboard, "Billing & invoices", "Currency & FX" — none of which claim 1 counts, and above a role tier the repo does not have. Building s-pc as a tenant screen would be the wrong build; building it correctly requires a platform-operator role and an authorization boundary that does not exist yet.
findings.fix: Scope s-pc (and its three siblings) as a separate platform-operator console with its own role, and treat the tenant admin's Credits & billing as the read side of it.

findings.title: No GST or tax handling anywhere in the product
findings.proto: Price-config tax card: "GST rate (INR billing)" input 18 with % suffix, note "GST registration: 29ABCDE1234F1Z5"; toggle "Show prices inclusive of GST" (off — "Default: exclusive (GST added at checkout)"); toggle "Apply local tax for international currencies" (on — "Customers responsible for local VAT/GST"). Three .gst-note strips. Account flow: _scripts.js:2838 gstOf(p)=Math.floor(p*0.18), rendered as the "GST (18%)" line in #ac-os-gst and the total in #ac-os-total; seat flow _scripts.js:3298 buyTotals() adds Math.round(sub*0.18) and renders "GST (18%)" + "Total · annual".
findings.repo: NONE. `grep -rni "gst" src migrations` matches only seed deck copy about a fictional GST-filing startup (migrations/0010_seed_workbench.sql:41). BuyCreditsPage.tsx:110 shows the bare pack price with no tax line.
findings.gap: Prices are shown tax-free with no GST line, no configurable rate, no inclusive/exclusive switch, no GSTIN, and no international "excl. local taxes" notice.
findings.fix: Add tax config (rate, GSTIN, inclusive flag, international-notice flag) to the pricing store; compute and display a GST line and gross total wherever a price is shown; keep the rate configurable rather than a literal 0.18.

findings.title: Clarification questions are generated ad hoc from area labels, not from a bank
findings.proto: admin/s-qb.html sub-title 'These questions are auto-triggered to the startup when the AI detects weak, missing, or contradictory signal in a given area'; 68 curated questions per area.
findings.repo: src/shared/queries.ts:35-49 areasNeedingResponse() returns bare labels; :52-68 buildQueryMessage() emits '• Traction & Validation (weak signal)' bullets in a fixed letter; src/client/routes/QueryPage.tsx:145-149 pre-fills the textarea with it; stored as one blob (migrations/0001_init.sql:123-131, src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:495-531).
findings.gap: The founder is told WHICH area is weak but never asked the specific BRD question. The 'targeted questions' the prototype promises do not exist.
findings.fix: Look up the weak areas' bank questions and compose the default body from them, grouped by area name, still editable before send.

findings.title: Per-area AI guidance prompt missing; only one org-wide prompt exists
findings.proto: admin/_scripts.js:264 RB_PROMPTS — 16 seeded per-key prompts; rbPromptHTML() (_scripts.js:266-271) renders label 'AI guidance prompt — what should the AI look for?' + textarea above the bands, swapped by rbLoad() on every dropdown change. live/specs/incubator.html §6.1: 'Each area also has an AI extraction prompt (per-area)'.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/ConfigPage.tsx:333-372 AiPromptSection — ONE textarea for the whole org (org_settings.ai_system_prompt, migrations/0001_init.sql:23; PUT /api/config/ai-prompt at src/server/routes/config.ts:331). Column parameters.prompt exists (migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:18) but is seeded NULL for the core 13 and is never editable for them.
findings.gap: An admin cannot tell the AI what to look for in Climate Impact specifically — only append one blanket paragraph to the system prompt.
findings.fix: Expose parameters.prompt for the core 13 in the rb editor, seed the 13 RB_PROMPTS strings, and add the p1/p2/p3 role-level prompts.

findings.title: Even when set, a core parameter's prompt is ignored by the evaluator
findings.proto: admin/s-rb.html sec-sub — the prompt is stated to guide the evaluation for that area; RB_PROMPTS covers a1..a13.
findings.repo: src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:312-326 — core params render as `- ${p.key} — ${p.name} (weight ${p.weight})` with no prompt; only `additional` (informational) params get `Guidance: ${p.prompt}` at 322-326.
findings.gap: parameters.prompt is silently dropped for the core 13, so seeding per-area prompts would have no effect on scoring until buildUserPrompt is changed.
findings.fix: Include each core parameter's prompt (with {{var}} substitution) in the core rubric block of buildUserPrompt, falling back to name+weight when null.

findings.title: Repo uses a 4-band anchor scale (8-10/5-7/2-4/0-1); the BRD/prototype scale is 5 bands (9-10/7-8/5-6/3-4/0-2)
findings.proto: admin/s-rb.html disabled Scale select 'BRD 5-band (0–2 · 3–4 · 5–6 · 7–8 · 9–10)'; admin/_scripts.js:263 RUBRICS has exactly 5 bands per key. live/specs/incubator.html §7: 'v≥9 Exceptional, v≥7 Strong, v≥5 Moderate, v≥3 Weak, else Insufficient'.
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:43-49 (comment literally says '0-1 / 2-4 / 5-7 / 8-10'); migrations/0002_seed.sql:5-9 seeds 4 rows strong/moderate/weak/absent; src/shared/scoring.ts:21-26 signalTag() uses >=8 / >=5 / >=2.
findings.gap: Wrong number of bands and wrong cut-points. A 7.5 is 'moderate' in the repo but 'Strong' per the BRD; a 2.5 is 'weak' in the repo but 'Insufficient' per the BRD. This band is fed to the AI (evaluate.ts:313-317) and drives deck signal colouring app-wide.
findings.fix: Replace the 4 bands with the 5 BRD bands (labels Exceptional/Strong/Moderate/Weak/Insufficient) and update signalTag() cut-points to >=9/>=7/>=5/>=3.

findings.title: Repo contradicts itself: analytics already uses the correct 5 bands while scoring/anchors use 4
findings.proto: admin/_scripts.js:263 RUBRICS — one 5-band scale used everywhere in the prototype.
findings.repo: src/shared/analytics.ts:181-187 bands '9–10 Exceptional','7–8 Strong','5–6 Moderate','3–4 Weak','0–2 Absent' vs src/shared/scoring.ts:21-26 signalTag() 4-band and migrations/0002_seed.sql:5-9.
findings.gap: The cohort score-distribution chart buckets decks on one scale while the deck's own signal badge is computed on another, so a deck can read '7–8 Strong' in the distribution and 'moderate' on its row. Also '0–2 Absent' vs the spec's 'Insufficient'.
findings.fix: Make analytics.ts consume the same band table as scoring.ts; rename the 0–2 label to 'Insufficient'.

findings.title: 'Configurable parameter anchors' block (AI+/AI++/AI+++) has no counterpart
findings.proto: admin/s-rb.html #rb-params + admin/_scripts.js:284-305 rbParamsRender() — 3 cards, each with role name, an 'ab ab-p' tier pill AI+/AI++/AI+++, an AI guidance prompt textarea, 5 band textareas, and a 'Save anchors' button.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:147-240 ParamRow — label + 'AI extraction prompt' only; no bands, no tier pill. src/server/routes/config.ts:215-311 additional-params routes accept {name, prompt, roleScope} only.
findings.gap: The three role-owned parameter groups have no rubric anchors at all, and the AI+/AI++/AI+++ tier identity the prototype attaches to them is absent.
findings.fix: Add a per-owner-role anchor set (5 bands + prompt) to MyParamsPage/the rb section and render the tier pill.

findings.title: Anchors are a single global 4-row table, not per-parameter anchor text
findings.proto: admin/_scripts.js:263 RUBRICS is keyed a1..a13,p1..p3 with a distinct free-text descriptor per band per area (65 seeded strings, e.g. a1 9–10 'Mission-critical problem with regulatory or economic pressure.'); admin/s-rb.html #rb-area re-renders #rb-bands per key. live/specs/incubator.html §7: 'Store as ParameterRubricBand(parameter_id, band_label, description)'.
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:44-49 rubric_anchors(band PRIMARY KEY, min_score, max_score, label) — one global row per band, `label` is a 2-word tag ('Strong signal'), no parameter_id and no description. src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:447-460 shows the same 4 generic bands for every parameter.
findings.gap: Every evaluation area shows the identical generic anchors. The prototype's whole point — that '9–10' means something different for Climate Impact than for Storytelling — cannot be expressed.
findings.fix: Add parameter_rubric_bands(parameter_id, band_label, min, max, description) with 16×5 rows seeded from RUBRICS; have EvaluatePage and the AI prompt read the selected parameter's bands.

findings.title: AI engine behaviour — all five toggles absent at every layer
findings.proto: admin/s-fw.html card `AI engine behaviour` (ti-cpu): `AI pre-scoring enabled` ON, `Auto-trigger clarification questions` ON, `Show AI score to jury before they score` ON, `Require override rationale` ON, `Jury can see each other's scores` OFF
findings.repo: NONE. migrations/0001_init.sql:18-26 org_settings holds only plan, credits_balance, branding_json, ai_system_prompt, threshold_best, threshold_mediocre (+criteria_version, 0009:14). src/server/routes/config.ts:20-27 SettingsRow mirrors that. src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:565-568 reads only ai_system_prompt. Repo-wide grep for pre-scoring/prescoring/blind/"override rationale" returns nothing.
findings.gap: Five org-wide AI-behaviour switches with defaults are specified; none is stored, exposed or honoured. The AI path is unconditional.
findings.fix: Add five boolean columns to org_settings with the prototype defaults (true/true/true/true/false), expose them on GET /api/config and a PUT /api/config/scoring-framework, and branch on them in the enqueue path, the query loop, the ai-scores read, the evaluate submit and the report matrix.

findings.title: Score composition — scale, formula and AI/Jury split have no setting and the composite is hard-coded
findings.proto: admin/s-fw.html card `Score composition` (ti-calculator): selects `Score scale` (0–10 default / 1–5 / 0–100), `Composite formula` (Weighted average default / Unweighted average / Median), `AI weight in composite` (40% AI · 60% Jury default / 30·70 / 50·50 / 0% jury only)
findings.repo: NONE for all three. src/shared/scoring.ts:11-16 weightedTotal is a fixed weighted average; :62 decisionScore hard-codes `(ai + human) / 2` — a 50/50 split, not the prototype's 40/60 default. src/server/config/rescore.ts:78 recomputes with the same fixed formula. Repo grep for scoreScale/score_scale/aiWeight/ai_weight/composite formula → nothing; `median` appears only in VC check-size analytics (shared/analytics.ts:482).
findings.gap: Three composition controls, each with a named default, are absent; the shipped AI/Jury split silently differs from the prototype default.
findings.fix: Store scale, formula and ai_weight on org_settings; thread them through shared/scoring.ts (weightedTotal + decisionScore), config/rescore.ts, the AI tool schema bounds and the rubric anchor bands; bump criteria_version on change and re-score.

findings.title: Score transparency & reports — all five toggles absent
findings.proto: admin/s-fw.html card `Score transparency & reports` (ti-eye), five toggles all ON: `Show 3-score view (AI · Mine · Average)`, `Show score drift analysis in reports`, `Include AI evidence quotes in reports`, `Mentor can adjust composite after all jury complete`, `Intro call AI question prompts enabled`
findings.repo: Two of the five behaviours exist but are unconditional and un-configurable: EvalScorecard.tsx:160-216 always renders the AI/My/Avg tiles and columns; nav.ts:99,103 + server/routes/analytics.ts:151-169 give drift its own report screen. The other three have no counterpart. No toggle for any of them.
findings.gap: The admin cannot turn any of the five on or off; three of the five behaviours do not exist at all.
findings.fix: Add five booleans to org_settings (all default true) and gate the workbench columns, the drift block, the AI evidence quotes, the mentor adjustment and the intro-call prompt generation on them.

findings.title: Blind scoring is not implementable today — the AI score is always served before the juror scores
findings.proto: admin/s-fw.html toggle `Show AI score to jury before they score` — sub `Turn off for blind independent jury evaluation`
findings.repo: src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:89 unconditionally loads the AI per-parameter map into `aiScores`; src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:163-168 always renders the `AI Score` tile and :214,:275 the `AI` column. Server serves the AI breakdown with no submitted-yet check (routes/decks.ts ai-scores read). Repo grep for `blind` → nothing.
findings.gap: No blind-scoring concept exists in schema or code; the AI number is visible to the juror at all times, which is the opposite of the toggle's OFF state.
findings.fix: Add the flag, and when it is off refuse the AI-breakdown read for a (deck, evaluator) pair with no submitted evaluation — server-side, not merely hidden in the client — then reveal after submit.

findings.title: Require override rationale — storage seam exists, the rule and the UI field do not
findings.proto: admin/s-fw.html toggle `Require override rationale` — sub `Jury must explain overrides greater than 2 points from AI score`
findings.repo: Seam present: migrations/0001_init.sql:92 `scores.comment TEXT`; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:361-395 accepts and persists a per-parameter comment; src/client/api.ts:399-403 HumanScoreInput carries an optional `comment`. Missing: src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:125 and :143 build the payload as `{ key, value }` only — no comment input is rendered anywhere, and no code compares a human value to the AI value.
findings.gap: The column and route exist but nothing writes them from the jury path, and the ±2-point delta rule that would make the rationale mandatory is absent.
findings.fix: Render a rationale textarea per parameter in EvalScorecard, send it as `comment`, and when the flag is on refuse a submit where |human − ai| > 2 and the comment is blank (validate in pipeline.ts, not just the client).

findings.title: Auto-trigger clarification questions — the loop exists but is entirely manual
findings.proto: admin/s-fw.html toggle `Auto-trigger clarification questions` — sub `Send targeted questions to startup when AI detects weak signal`
findings.repo: Manual loop present: src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:436-490 (queries per deck, founder answer re-enters intake), src/client/routes/QueryPage.tsx:30-64, src/server/email/outbox.ts:223, default copy at src/shared/queries.ts:51-58. findings.title: The sign-up sub-status enum (initiated → progress → completed → onboarded) does not exist — the repo models the whole sign-up as one hop
findings.proto: specs/incubator.html §Key enums: 'Sign-up / pipeline status: shortlisted, rejected, initiated, progress, completed, onboarded, archived'; §8.2: 'initiated → progress → completed → onboarded is the sign-up happy path'. The prototype's four workspace stages are computed directly from these values — AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:2013-2020 suSignupBody maps sg==='initiated' → Founder response active, sg==='progress' → Verify & countersign active, after(['completed','onboarded','archived']) → Completed done — and the seatless card at :2050-2055 renders only once sg is 'completed', with suAllocSeat (:2069) advancing it to 'onboarded'.
findings.repo: src/pipeline/incubator.ts:24-25 defines exactly two sign-up statuses, `signup` and `onboard_ready` (terminal), and :123/:130 exactly two actions, `send_signup` and `complete_signup`. src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:352-353 renders the 'Sign-up status' column as a bare `deck.status` string — there is no initiated / progress / completed value anywhere in src/ or migrations/. No sign-up token table either (`grep -rniE "signup.?token|signup.?link|/signup/" src/ migrations/` returns nothing), so the prototype's emailed https://startupjury.in/signup/<token> link has no counterpart, though resubmit_tokens (migrations/0017) is the working pattern.
findings.gap: Claims 9 and 14 report the missing seat flag and the missing workspace, but not the state model both stand on. Without intermediate states a deck cannot be 'completed but seatless' (the exact predicate claim 9's badge is defined on), the four workspace stage chips have nothing to drive them, and 'documents submitted, awaiting countersign' is indistinguishable from 'invite just sent'. This should be sequenced before the seat and workspace work rather than discovered during it.
findings.fix: Extend the incubator pipeline with initiated / progress / completed between `signup` and `onboard_ready` (or hold them on a `signups.status` column so the deck status stays coarse), drive the workspace stage chips and the seatless predicate from it, and mint a tokenized founder sign-up link modelled on resubmit_tokens.

findings.title: Per-area scoring is whole-number only; the spec mandates 0.5 steps
findings.proto: incubator/vc spec §7 Scoring & Aggregation, first line: 'Per-area score: **integer/half-step 0–10 (step 0.5)**. AI supplies a suggested value; the human can override.' This is the spec-side counterpart of the s-fw 'Score scale' control the auditor reported as missing (claim 3), but it is a behavioural requirement rather than a settings one.
findings.repo: src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:245-248 `<input type="range" min={0} max={10} step={1}>` for core parameters, and :303-306 the identical control for additional parameters — the only two score inputs in the app. Nothing else in src/client/components/*.tsx sets a step. The storage layer is fine (migrations/0001_init.sql:91 `value REAL`) and the server clamps but does not round (pipeline.ts:371 `Math.max(0, Math.min(10, …))`), so this is purely the input granularity.
findings.gap: An evaluator cannot express a 7.5. Since the spec's five-band mapping puts boundaries at whole numbers (v≥9, v≥7, v≥5, v≥3), half-steps are the only way to score within a band, and the claim-3 'Score scale' control would be meaningless without the underlying granularity.
findings.fix: Set step={0.5} on both range inputs and format the displayed value to one decimal; no schema or server change is needed.

findings.title: Panel 4's summary card is a different artefact: no deck chips, no removable member chips, no 'N decks × M members = nE evaluations' scope row, no card header
findings.proto: panels/Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/_scripts.js:1150-1170 — renderAs4 builds `.as-summary-card` with a header ('Assignment summary' / 'Review before confirming' + icon tile) and four labelled rows: Decks (a `.as-deck-chip` per selected deck), Jury members (a `.as-mem-chip` per member carrying avatar, name, uppercase role and an `×` that calls `asRemoveMember(key)` — _scripts.js:1050-1054), Scope ('N decks × M jury members = nE evaluations'), Deadline. The empty state (_scripts.js:1143-1147) is also two-stage: 'Select at least one deck from column 1.' then 'Pick one or more jury members from column 3 — you can mix roles.'
findings.repo: src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx:295-336 — a `u-label` header 'Assignment summary', then a flat `<ul>` of one row per deck reading `deck.name` over `member.name · title`, then a single sentence 'N decks across M members (spread evenly)'. No chips, no per-member remove control, no scope arithmetic, no deadline row, and one static empty state (:297-304).
findings.gap: Beyond the round-robin semantics (claim 1), the panel-4 SHAPE differs: the prototype reviews the selection as two chip sets with a removable member control and states the resulting evaluation count, whereas the repo lists the computed pairs. The 'mix roles' behaviour the empty state promises is also absent — repo `memberIds` is reset on every `pickRole` (AssignPage.tsx:88-92), so members from two different roles can never be selected together, while prototype `asChosen` is keyed `roleIdx-userIdx` and deliberately spans roles (_scripts.js:1041-1046).
findings.fix: Rebuild panel 4 as the prototype's summary card (deck chips, removable member chips with role, scope row, deadline row) and keep member selections across role switches.

findings.proto: _scripts.js:241-247 — every qFounders row carries a flags string ('3 areas need input' … '1 area needs input') and a non-empty `areas` array; panel-query.html:223 `.pnl-topbar-sub` 'AI-flagged decks awaiting founder clarification'

findings.gap: QUERYABLE_STATUSES.vc is `["incomplete", "analyst_scoring", "associate_review"]` (QueryPage.tsx:35-36) and rows are filtered on deck stage alone (:127-130). Two consequences. First, `"incomplete"` is not a VC stage at all — src/pipeline/vc.ts:10-24 declares uploaded, pending_ai, analyst_scoring, associate_review, partner_review, partner_call, investment_dd, ic_review, mp_decision, alignment_call, term_sheet, legal_dd, onboard_ready, archived, with no `incomplete` entry — so that clause is dead on VC. The prototype's list is a queue of decks that actually need founder input; the VC repo list is a stage dump.
findings.fix: Filter the VC rows to decks that actually have something to ask about — `areasNeedingResponse(deck).length > 0` or an open query row — rather than by stage membership alone, and reconcile the dead `incomplete` status with the VC stage list.

Three elements here appear nowhere else in the prototype and nowhere in the repo: the deck-completion progress bar with the 'N of M areas sufficient' breakdown, the explicit 'areas that are FINE' roster (the repo only ever lists what is wrong — QueryPage.tsx:517-537 and ResubmitPage.tsx:180-217 both render deficits only), and the readiness checklist that tells the founder what still blocks submission. That question should go to the client rather than be assumed either way.
findings.fix: Confirm with the client whether VIEW B is live. If it is, the reusable parts are the completion meter and the 'sufficient signal' roster on ResubmitPage (both derivable from the existing scores-vs-threshold_mediocre query at src/server/routes/decks.ts:65).

findings.title: The whole page scrolls in the repo; the prototype's fixed-frame shell (pinned panel toolbar, pinned footer stat+legend bar, 278px right rail) has no counterpart
findings.proto: Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/_style.css: `.view{height:100vh;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden}` → `.ab{display:flex;flex:1;overflow:hidden}` → `.mn{flex:1;display:flex;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden}`, and 21 of 22 panel roots are `<div id="panel-*" style="display:none;flex:1;flex-direction:column;overflow:hidden">`. Scrolling is confined to an inner region: `.su-scroll{flex:1;overflow:auto}` / `.dp{flex:1;overflow-y:auto;padding:12px 16px}`. Above it `.su-tb{padding:11px 18px;background:var(--surface);border-bottom:1px solid var(--stone-dk);flex-shrink:0}` holds title+sub+toolbar buttons; below it `.su-foot{flex-shrink:0;padding:10px 18px;border-top:1px solid var(--stone);background:var(--surface)}` holds `.su-foot-stat` (count) on the left and `.su-legend` (colour dots) on the right — see panel-forsignup.html, panel-incuration.html, panel-alldecks.html. `.rp{width:278px;min-width:278px;border-left:1px solid var(--stone-dk);overflow-y:auto;background:var(--surface)}` is the shell's right rail.
findings.repo: src/client/components/AppShell.tsx:58 `<main className="min-w-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto">` — the entire routed page is the scroll container, and the shell offers no right-rail slot. src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:448 `<div className="flex flex-col gap-5 p-5">` — title, subtitle and Export scroll away with the table; StagePage.tsx:553-562 renders the legend as an ordinary flow element BENEATH the table instead of in a pinned footer, and the row count is a `<Badge tone="info">` beside the title (StagePage.tsx:456) rather than a `.su-foot-stat` line.
findings.gap: In the prototype the chrome is fixed and only the data region moves: the page title/subtitle/Filter/Export strip is a white bordered bar pinned to the top of the panel, and the count + colour legend is a white bordered bar pinned to the bottom, with the table scrolling between them (and, where used, a 278px right pane beside it). In the repo nothing is pinned — the header, table and legend are one long scrolling column on the page background, the toolbar disappears as soon as the user scrolls a long table, and the legend is only reachable by scrolling past every row. This is the single most-repeated layout in both editions (10 of 22 incubator panels and 11 of 30 VC panels use the su- frame outright, and every remaining panel uses the same overflow:hidden + inner-scroll pattern), so it affects essentially every screen.
findings.fix: Give the shell a fixed frame: make <main> `overflow-hidden` and introduce a shared PanelFrame (sticky bordered header on --surface holding title/subtitle/toolbar, a `flex-1 overflow-auto` body, and an optional pinned footer taking the stat line + legend), plus an optional right-rail slot. Then convert StagePage / CallsPage / the report screens onto it.

findings.repo: src/client/index.css:27-36 — only signal-strong/moderate/weak/absent/flagged plus --color-info exist; no purple, no ink, no -lt tint tokens, no gold-dk.
findings.gap: The repo approximates every tinted status background with a `/12` alpha of a signal colour, and has no purple at all (the prototype uses it for the avatar and the `.r-adm` role pill), so status pills differ in hue from the prototype (e.g. red #c0392b vs #DC2626, green #4a6644 vs #16A34A).

findings.title: Neutral ramp is cooler and one step shorter than the prototype's
findings.proto: `_style.css:1` `--offwht:#F7F6F2;--stone:#ECEAE4;--stone-dk:#D4D0C8;--text:#1A1E2E;--text-2:#4A4840;--text-3:#9A9488;--navy:#1A1E2E`.
findings.repo: src/client/index.css:43-48 `--bg:#f5f7f2; --line:#d8ddd2; --fg:#1a1a2e; --fg-muted:#888888`; index.css:17 `--color-navy:#1a1a2e`.
findings.gap: The prototype's neutrals are warm (beige/taupe: offwht F7F6F2, stone ECEAE4, text-3 9A9488); the repo's are cool green-grey (F5F7F2, D8DDD2, 888888). There is also no `--stone` (soft border) — the repo has one `--line` for both `--stone` and `--stone-dk` — and no `--text-2` mid tone, only fg and fg-muted. `--navy` differs in the third byte (#1A1E2E vs #1a1a2e).
findings.fix: Retune the neutrals to the prototype hexes and add a `--fg-2` mid tone and a soft `--line-soft` matching `--stone`.

findings.title: No panel toolbar bar — every screen uses an in-flow h1 on the page background

findings.repo: 24 occurrences of `<h1 className="text-xl font-semibold text-fg">` across src/client/routes (e.g. DashboardPage.tsx:238, StagePage.tsx, AnalyticsKit.tsx:44); grep for `sticky top-0` in src/client returns nothing.
findings.gap: The prototype's persistent white toolbar strip with a hairline under it — the element that visually anchors every screen — is replaced by a 20px heading that sits on the page background and scrolls away.
findings.fix: Add a shared PageToolbar component (surface bg, bottom hairline, 13.5px title + 10.5px sub, right-aligned .tbb buttons) and use it on every routed screen.

findings.title: The entire avatar profile dropdown is missing

findings.title: The 900px icon-rail sidebar tier is missing; breakpoints differ
findings.proto: `_style.css:280-306` `@media (max-width:900px){.sb{width:52px;min-width:52px} .sb .sbl,.sf{display:none} .si{padding:8px;justify-content:center} .si i{font-size:16px;opacity:1} .si span,.si .bx{display:none} .sb .sgrp-head{display:none} .tbr .tbb:not(.pr){display:none} .sr{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr)}}` then `:309` the ≤640px drawer.

findings.gap: The prototype has three tiers (full → 52px icon rail → drawer). The repo has two, at a different pivot: 640–768px gets a drawer where the prototype gives an icon rail, and 768–900px gets a full 240px rail where the prototype gives 52px icons. Toolbar-button collapsing at 900px is also absent.

findings.title: No toast system for action confirmations

findings.gap: 36 prototype actions confirm with a transient toast; in the repo most of those actions give either an inline badge or no feedback at all.
findings.fix: Add a small toast provider matching the prototype's styling and call it from the mutation handlers.

findings.title: No global toast/confirmation surface; the prototype confirms 14 distinct actions with one

findings.gap: Every state-changing action the prototype acknowledges with a toast (send signup, shortlist, reject, schedule, save, delegate, …) completes silently in the repo unless the individual screen happened to add its own inline message. The prototype also shows a notification bell (``) in the top bar of all 11 role files, which the repo's Topbar does not render at all.
findings.fix: Add a small toast provider mounted in AppShell and call it from the shared action handlers in StagePage/CallsPage/EvaluatePage; add the bell to Topbar (even if it only routes somewhere) so the ribbon matches.

findings.title: Sidebar drops the prototype's count badges, its nested Evaluation sub-group and its 900px icon rail
findings.proto:
_sidebar.html: `
All decks24
` — a count badge on All decks in ALL 11 role files (the VC IC member's reads 9), plus a red ticket badge `` on Tickets in the SU/Admin files. `.bx{margin-left:auto;font-size:9.5px;font-weight:600;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:9px}` / `.bx-b{background:var(--blue-lt);color:var(--blue)}`. Hierarchy: Evaluation is a NESTED `

Responsive: `@media (max-width:900px){.sb{width:52px;min-width:52px}.sb .sbl{display:none}.si{padding:8px;justify-content:center}.si i{font-size:16px}.si span,.si .bx{display:none}.sb .sgrp-head{display:none}}` — an always-visible 52px icon rail between 641 and 900px.
findings.repo: src/client/components/Sidebar.tsx:66-119 — the NavLink renders only an active bar, an icon and a truncated label; there is no badge element and NavItem (src/shared/nav.ts:1-40) carries no count/badge field. Sections come from a flat `NAV_SECTIONS` list (nav.ts:193-201) grouped at Sidebar.tsx:59-64, so Evaluation renders as a sibling of Workflows with no indent or left rule. src/client/components/AppShell.tsx:36 `hidden w-60 … md:block` + :41-56 drawer — the sidebar is either a full 240px panel (≥768px) or hidden behind the hamburger (<768px); there is no intermediate icon-rail tier anywhere in src/client.

findings.proto: VC_Final_files_AISJ_VC_Superuser_V6_html/panel-alldecks.html:32-37 (the VC labels sit on the incubator data-stat keys all/pending/incomplete/evaluated/assigned/shortlisted) + _scripts.js:79-86 `adData` (each deck's `st` string assigns it to In Diligence / IC ready / Onboard ready buckets) and _scripts.js:94-99 (adRenderTable's list filter)

findings.gap: The auditor's claim 2 covers labels, sublabels and order but not what each tile SELECTS. In the repo the 4th tile filters `aiScore !== undefined`, the 5th filters `assignedTo || statusId in [assigned, jury_evaluation, analyst_scoring, associate_review]`, and the 6th (`shortlisted`) matches nine VC stages from partner_review through onboard_ready. The VC prototype's 4th/5th/6th tiles mean In Diligence (investment_dd), IC ready (ic_review) and Onboard ready (onboard_ready) — single pipeline positions. So renaming the tiles alone would produce correct captions over wrong row sets: 'Onboard ready' would list every deal past partner review, and 'In Diligence' would list every AI-scored deck in the fund. The counts on the tiles are wrong for the same reason.
findings.fix: Make STAT_ORDER and matchesStat edition-keyed: give VC its own six definitions (Uploaded=all; Incomplete=statusId 'incomplete'; AI Evaluated=aiScore present; In Diligence=investment_dd; IC ready=ic_review; Onboard ready=onboard_ready) with the VC sublabels, and keep pipelineProgress deriving from the same list.

findings.title: VC Evaluate lists the wrong pool of decks — the decks the screen exists to queue can never appear on it
findings.proto: VC_Final_files_AISJ_VC_Superuser_V6_html/_scripts.js:425-433 `evDecks` (every uploaded deck, each with `ai`, `flags` and a `done` flag), :507-511 `addToEvaluate()`, and :641-648 `upUploadSelected()` — the Upload screen pushes each complete deck onto the Evaluate list; renderEvDecks then badges it with N flags / 'Evaluated'

findings.gap: Distinct from the missing batch UI (claim 6): the underlying data set is wrong. The prototype's Evaluate is the queue of decks that have been uploaded and are waiting to be sent for AI scoring, fed directly by Upload. The repo gates the list to three human-scoring stages, so decks at `pending_ai`, `incomplete` or `intake` — exactly the ones an operator would want to queue — are invisible on Evaluate, and there is no repo screen anywhere that offers 'send these decks for AI evaluation' (grep for 'Evaluate selected' / 'Send for evaluation' across src/ returns nothing; the only batch AI path is UploadPage's bulk upload, which enqueues automatically with no operator gate).

findings.proto: Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/_rest.html:1396 — '#fp-login … Sign in with the email this request was sent to' plus the 'Registered email' field at :1397-1398 presupposes a founder identity that exists and is keyed on the address the query was mailed to; _scripts.js:3170-3172 resolves the founder by identity (`qFounders[i]`, each row carrying its own `email`).
findings.repo: src/shared/roles.ts:204-211 — `creatableStaffRoles` filters out 'founder' with the comment 'founders are external self-registrants, not staff created by an admin', and src/server/routes/users.ts:134-137/:240-242 rejects any non-creatable role with 400 invalid_role; NO self-registration exists — grep for register|/signup|sign_up across src/server/routes/*.ts and src/server/index.ts returns nothing, and src/server/routes/auth.ts has only login/logout/session; the only founder row in the product is migrations/0002_seed.sql:50 ('inc_founder', Meera Sharma), whose visible decks are hand-wired in migrations/0005_seed_founder_decks.sql:7-8.
findings.gap: The comment in roles.ts promises a self-registration path that was never built, and user management is explicitly barred from creating the role, so there is no mechanism — admin-side or founder-side — to give a real founder credentials. This is the root cause sitting underneath the sign-in claim and the uploaded_by-scoping claim: even if both were fixed, no founder would have an account to sign in with. The portal is reachable today only by logging in as the seeded demo founder.
findings.fix: Pick one and build it: (a) provision a founder account automatically when a deck's founder_email is captured at intake, mailing a set-password or one-time-code link (this also supplies the prototype's access-code flow); or (b) add founder to creatableStaffRoles with an invite flow on the Query/Upload screens. Either way, bind the account to decks by founder_email, not uploaded_by.
