findings.title: Querying several founders at once sends all of them one merged message built from the union of every selected deck's flagged areas — contradicting the on-screen promise that each founder sees only their own
findings.proto: Incubator_Final_files_AISJ_IC_SuserV11_HTM/panel-query.html:269 ('Recipients reflect your current selection — go back to the list to add or remove founders') and :293-298 ('Link the founder receives'); _scripts.js:3170-3172 `fpBuild(i)` builds each founder's form from `qFounders[i].areas` — that founder's own areas only — and :3178-3184 renders exactly those. The prototype's model is one personalised question set per founder.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/QueryPage.tsx:147-149 — when more than one deck is selected, `const shared = selected.flatMap((d) => areasNeedingResponse(d))` then `setBody(buildQueryMessage("your pitch deck", shared))`, i.e. one message from the pooled areas of every selected deck; :168-172 — `sendQuery` loops the selected decks posting that same `body` to each (`const message = [subject, "", body].join("\n")` is hoisted from one shared state); :420-423 — the copy under the composer reads 'Each founder receives their own copy listing only their areas requiring response … Founders never see another startup's query.'
findings.gap: Select five decks and every founder receives an identical list containing the other four startups' flagged areas. Founder A is asked to explain traction gaps their own deck does not have, and learns the aggregate weak spots of the batch. There is no per-recipient rendering step anywhere: `buildQueryMessage` is called once for the pooled selection, and the loop reuses the result. The screen states the opposite in two sentences, so the defect is invisible to the operator sending it.
findings.fix: Move message generation inside the send loop — call `buildQueryMessage(deck.name, areasNeedingResponse(deck))` per deck and post that — and change the composer for a multi-select into a per-recipient preview (or an editable template with per-founder area substitution) rather than one shared textarea.

findings.title: The prototype dispatches every selected deck to EVERY selected member (deck × member); the repo can only give a deck ONE assignee, so it round-robins instead
findings.proto: VC SU _scripts.js:1144-1157 asConfirm() — `selectedDecks.forEach(d => members.forEach(mem => rows.push({...})))`, i.e. N×M dispatch rows; renderAs4() at :1188 states the contract in the UI: "N decks × M jury members = N×M evaluations". findings.repo: src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx:70-76 (`selectedDecks.map((deck, i) => ({ deck, member: selectedMembers[i % selectedMembers.length] }))`) and the acknowledging comment at AssignPage.tsx:20-22 ("…because a deck carries one assignee"); the constraint is in the schema — migrations/0001_init.sql:64 `assigned_to TEXT REFERENCES users (id)` (one column), written by src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:296 `UPDATE decks SET … assigned_to = ?`.
findings.gap: The design's core assignment semantics are inverted. In the prototype, ticking 3 decks and 4 members creates 12 evaluations — every member evaluates every deck, which is what makes the pipeline's multi-juror score column and the AI-vs-jury drift comparison meaningful. The repo splits 3 decks across 4 members (3 evaluations, one evaluator per deck), because `decks.assigned_to` is a single foreign key. This is not a UI difference: rebuilding the Submit screen as specified is impossible without a deck↔evaluator join table, so it is a prerequisite for the P0 in claim 1 rather than a follow-up to it.
findings.fix: Introduce a `deck_assignments (deck_id, evaluator_id, assigned_at, deadline_at, instructions)` table, make the assign endpoint accept a member LIST, and derive `assigned_to`/`assigned_at` from it for backward compatibility. Then panel 4's "N × M = X evaluations" and the results table's one-row-per-dispatch layout follow naturally.

findings.title: A VC deck can be set to status 'incomplete', but the VC pipeline defines no such stage — the deck becomes a dead end with a raw lowercase label and zero available actions

findings.repo: src/pipeline/vc.ts:9-26 — the VC `stages` array has no `incomplete` entry (the incubator's is at src/pipeline/incubator.ts:18); src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:417-420 `computeResult` returns `status: "incomplete"` with no edition check and evaluate.ts:721 mails the founder about it; src/server/routes/decks.ts:139-141 `statusLabel` falls back to the raw id when getStage() misses; src/client/routes/QueryPage.tsx:36 lists `"incomplete"` for the VC edition.
findings.gap: When the AI cannot score a VC deck, `computeResult` parks it at `status='incomplete'`. `getStage('vc','incomplete')` returns undefined, so (a) every screen shows the literal lowercase string "incomplete" instead of a stage label, (b) `allowedTransitions` finds nothing, so the deck has zero action buttons anywhere, and (c) nothing in vc.ts can move it back — the incubator's `incomplete → uploaded` resubmit transition (incubator.ts:65) has no VC twin. The deck is permanently stuck, which is the functional half of the incomplete/Query loop the Submit screen is supposed to drive. The auditor reported the missing UI (claim 3) but not that the underlying stage does not exist.
findings.fix: Add an `incomplete` stage to vc.ts plus the resubmit transition back to `uploaded`/`analyst_scoring`, mirroring incubator.ts:58-70.

findings.title: Assignment is a single FK, so a deck can only ever have one evaluator

The per-evaluator report columns the repo already built cannot be populated through the assignment flow.

findings.title: No pending/draft/submitted state and no all-parameters-scored gate
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #81-evaluation-lifecycle — "pending → (Save draft) → draft → (Submit, all parameters scored) → submitted. Submission is blocked until every applicable parameter has a score."
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:98-106 — `evaluations` has weighted_total, verdict, remarks, submitted_at; no `state` column, and no ALTER adds one (grep `ALTER TABLE evaluations` → only 0009's two version columns). src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:336 is a single `Save scores` button, disabled only while `busy`. src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:373 rejects only `clean.length === 0`, then src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:378-381 scores unscored parameters as 0 in the weighted total.

findings.fix: Add `evaluations.state`, split the button into Save draft / Submit, and reject a submit that is missing any applicable parameter.

findings.title: Four of the seven sign-up statuses do not exist

findings.title: The Assign confirm step fans out N decks × M members in the prototype; the repo allocates round-robin and drops the instructions, deadline and notify controls
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:1124-1135 `asConfirm()` — `selectedDecks.forEach(d => members.forEach(mem => rows.push(...)))`, an explicit cross-product. renderAs4() at :1160-1170 prints the summary card "Scope: <N> decks × <M> jury members = <N×M> evaluations" and "Deadline: 7 days from assignment date", plus an "Instructions to evaluators (optional)" textarea (as-instr-ta) and a "Notify <M> jury members by email" toggle (as-notify-row).
findings.repo: src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx:69-76 — `selectedDecks.map((deck,i) => ({deck, member: selectedMembers[i % selectedMembers.length]}))`, one member per deck, with the comment at :16-22 stating the rule is round-robin "because a deck carries one assignee". confirm() at :96-108 loops `assignDeck(deck.id, member.id)`; src/client/api.ts:392-397 `assignDeck(id, assigneeId)` takes a single assignee and no other payload. grep for instruction|deadline|notify|email over AssignPage.tsx returns nothing.
findings.gap: Selecting 5 decks and a 3-person panel produces 5 assignments in the repo and 15 in the prototype — the panel-of-jurors semantics that §7's jury aggregation depends on never happens. Three specified controls on the confirm panel (evaluator instructions, the 7-day deadline, the notify-by-email toggle) have no field, no column and no API parameter. The auditor treated the round-robin only as something that 'hides' the schema problem and did not report that the prototype specifies the opposite allocation rule or that these three controls are missing.

findings.title: The 13 core areas carry no per-area AI extraction prompt and no clarification-question set
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:439-451 — each of the 13 `evParams` entries carries its own `prompt` ('Does the problem matter, and to whom? Evaluate against the rubric anchors below. If signals are weak, missing, or contradictory, trigger the clarification questions for this area.') AND a five-item `criteria` array of clarification questions. :577-600 `evOpenParam(i)` renders the detail card as 'Evaluation prompt' (with Save / Configure buttons), 'AI clarification questions (asked when signals are weak)', then 'Rubric anchors'. Spec vc.html §6.1: 'Each area is scored 0–10, has a five-band rubric (§7), an AI-extraction prompt, and a weight defined in-file.'
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:16-18 states the intent plainly — the new `prompt` column is 'NULL for core areas, which fall back to name + weight'. src/server/routes/config.ts:151-190 `PUT /parameters` is the only core-parameter write and accepts nothing but `weight` and `name` (:174-178), so a core area's prompt can never be set or edited. src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:443 papers over the absence with a generated string: `{param.prompt ?? `Score ${param.name} from 0 to 10 against the rubric anchors below.`}`. There is one global prompt instead (config.ts:331-344 `PUT /ai-prompt` → org_settings.ai_system_prompt). Clarification questions do not exist at all: `grep -rni "criteria|question_bank|questionBank|clarification" src/ migrations/` (excluding criteria_version) finds only the free-text founder-query loop (pipeline.ts:436-490) — no per-area canned question set anywhere.
findings.gap: Two of the three things §6.1 says a standard area has are missing from the data model. The per-area extraction prompt — the thing that makes the AI's 13 scores auditable and fund-tunable — collapses to one workspace-wide system prompt plus an autogenerated sentence, and the five clarification questions per area that the prototype fires 'when signals are weak' have no storage, no seed and no editor. This is the same root cause as the rubric-band finding (claim 9) but a distinct missing field: even if the five bands were added, the prompt and the question bank would still be absent.
findings.fix: Add `prompt` seeding for the 13 core rows and a `parameter_questions` (or JSON column) table for the five clarification questions per area; extend `PUT /config/parameters` to accept prompt/questions alongside weight, and render them in the EvaluatePage parameter detail panel where the anchors already appear.

findings.title: The AI suggested score is never pre-filled as the human's starting value — every untouched parameter is submitted as a deliberate 5.0
findings.proto: spec §2: "the platform's AI pre-populates a suggested score (0–10) for each of the 13 standard evaluation areas … Human evaluators then review and override scores". spec §7: "AI supplies a suggested value; the human can override." spec §10: "AI pre-fills a suggested score using each parameter's prompt."
findings.repo: src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:109 — `setValues(Object.fromEntries(allScored.map((p) => [p.key, 5])))` on every deck selection, before loadDeckData runs; :86-97 loads the AI breakdown into a SEPARATE `aiScores` map that is only displayed, never merged into `values`; :125 and :143 then post `allScored.map(p => ({key: p.key, value: values[p.key] ?? 0}))` — all 13 core + up-to-3 additional, every time.
findings.gap: There is no override semantics at all: the human always starts from a flat 5 regardless of what the AI found, and an evaluator who opens a deck, writes a remark and clicks Save records a full, submitted, weighted evaluation of 5.0 across every parameter. That evaluation then feeds the deck's human average, the AI-vs-human drift report and the pipeline ranking as if it were real scoring. Combined with the absent draft state and completeness gate (claim 5), nothing in the product distinguishes a scored deck from an opened one.
findings.fix: Seed `values` from the AI suggestion once loadDeckData resolves (falling back to 5 only where the AI produced nothing), and track which parameters the human actually touched so the submit gate in claim 5 has something to check.

findings.title: Score inputs are locked to whole numbers; the spec and prototype both use 0.5 steps
findings.proto: spec §7: "Per-area score: integer/half-step 0–10 (step 0.5)". live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:3733, :3767 and :4288 — the active scoring inputs are emitted with `step="0.5"`.
findings.repo: src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:248 (core parameters) and :306 (additional parameters) — both range inputs are `min={0} max={10} step={1}`. These are the only two score inputs in the component.
findings.gap: An evaluator physically cannot enter 7.5, which the spec's band table treats as "Strong" and which the repo's own seeded human scores use (migrations/0024 stores 9.5, 8.5, 7.5 across five decks). The report renders those half-steps but the scorecard cannot reproduce them, so re-opening and re-saving a seeded evaluation silently rounds every half-step away.
findings.fix: Change step to 0.5 on both inputs in EvalScorecard.tsx and widen the value readout column (currently w-5, sized for one digit).

findings.title: Scoring is bound to neither a role nor a gate — any VC evaluator can score any deal in any of the three scoring stages
findings.proto: Spec vc.html §8.4: 'at each gate the current role's own parameters are editable; upstream roles' parameters are shown as read-only reference ("completed"); downstream sections are hidden until reached', and §5: 'Assignment links a deck to an evaluator and records the role lens and the pipeline stage; it gates whether a user gets an editable vs read-only workspace at that gate.' The prototype enforces this by opening the report from a specific pipeline panel with a specific role lens — e.g. _scripts.js:2134 opens it from panel-icpipeline with `role:'jury', roleName:'IC Member'` and the icScored flag, so only the IC block is editable there.
findings.repo: src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:50 `const VC_SCORING_STAGES = ["analyst_scoring", "associate_review", "partner_review"]` is ONE flat list applied to every VC role at :344-346, and the per-deck ownership check immediately above it is incubator-only: :339-342 `if (user.role === "jury" && deck.assigned_to !== user.id)`. requireRole at :325-333 admits analyst, associate, partner and ic_member equally. On the client, src/client/routes/VcEvaluatePage.tsx:60-63 `rows = decks.filter(d => SCORING_STAGES.includes(d.statusId))` applies no assignment filter and no role↔stage pairing, so every evaluator sees every deal in all three stages.
findings.gap: Nothing binds a role's lens to its gate. A partner can score at analyst_scoring, an analyst at partner_review, and (per the corrected claim 2) an IC member scores their IC lens during partner review — the one stage the spec reserves for the partner lens. Combined with the absence of an Assignment record, there is also no per-deck ownership on the VC side at all, so any evaluator can score any deal in the funnel. This is the enforcement half of §8.4 that the auditor's claim 3 (the missing Assign SCREEN and entity) and claim 7 (the non-stage-aware REPORT) each touch but neither states: even with the existing schema, the server permits wrong-role-at-wrong-gate writes today.
findings.fix: Derive the permitted (role, stage) pairs from src/pipeline/vc.ts rather than a flat stage list — e.g. analyst↔analyst_scoring, associate↔associate_review, partner↔partner_review, ic_member↔ic_review — reject a score whose role does not own the deal's current stage, and filter the Evaluate queue by the same pairing plus the assignment once it exists.

findings.title: Per-parameter evaluator remarks cannot be entered anywhere — the column exists, the UI never writes it
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:4295 — every core-parameter row expands to `<div class="jr-myrem"><label>My remarks for this parameter</label><textarea … oninput="jrRem(k,this.value)">`; :4497 `window.jrRem=function(k,val){ myRemarks[curName][k]=val; }`; :4502 `jrCustomRem` does the same for each additional parameter; :4382 the read-only `roAddl` block replays an upstream role's per-parameter remark. Spec vc.html §5: 'Evaluation 1───∞ EvaluationRemark (one per parameter, optional)' and §12 `evaluation_remarks(evaluation_id, parameter_id, remark)`; §13 `PATCH /evaluations/:id save draft (scores + remarks)'.
findings.repo: The storage and the API both exist: migrations/0001_init.sql:92 `scores.comment TEXT`; src/client/api.ts:399-403 `HumanScoreInput { key; value; comment?: string }`; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:371 `clean.push({ …, comment: s.comment ?? null })`. Nothing ever supplies it. src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx renders each parameter row with only a range input (:243-256 core, :300-311 additional) and offers exactly one whole-evaluation textarea at :324-332 ('Remarks (optional)'); src/client/routes/VcEvaluatePage.tsx:108 and src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:125,:143 all build the payload as `allScored.map((p) => ({ key: p.key, value: values[p.key] ?? 0 }))` with no comment. `grep -n comment` across those three files returns only READS of the AI's comment (EvalScorecard.tsx:230,:288).
findings.gap: A human evaluator can attach one note to the whole deck but cannot say anything about an individual parameter — the exact artefact the prototype's expander collects and the report replays as an upstream role's reference. Because `scores.comment` is populated only by the AI path (ai/evaluate.ts), the report's per-score tooltip (EvaluationReport.tsx:97) can only ever show AI text, never a colleague's reasoning. This is a pure 'API exists, no UI' gap: the column, the request type and the server write are all in place.
findings.fix: Add a per-row remark textarea (collapsed expander) to EvalScorecard for both the core and additional tables, thread it through `onChangeRemark(key, text)` into the `comment` field the payload already supports, and surface it in EvaluationReport's row expander instead of the title tooltip.

findings.screen: Jury Pipeline / Intro calls / Sign up Pipeline (StagePage "Jury score" column)
findings.title: The "Jury score" that ranks the pipeline averages every human evaluator, not the jury
findings.proto: spec §7: "Jury aggregation: across all jury evaluations of a deck, average the per-parameter scores (and the composite). This average is what ranks the pipeline." spec §12 aggregation views: "deck_jury_score = avg of jury evaluations.composite for a deck" and "deck_pipeline_rank = order by deck_jury_score within a program".
findings.repo: src/server/routes/decks.ts:58 — `(SELECT AVG(e.weighted_total) FROM evaluations e WHERE e.deck_id = d.id AND e.evaluator_id IS NOT NULL) AS human_avg` — no join to users, no role filter. decks.ts:236 exposes it as `juryScore`; decks.ts:197-200 feeds the same value into `decisionScore(ai, [human_avg])` as the deck's decision score. src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:88 labels the column "Jury score" and it appears on jurypipeline, pmpipeline, introcalls and incuration (lines 602, 612, 677, 694, 713).
findings.gap: A Program Associate's or Program Manager's or Admin's evaluation is folded into the number displayed and sorted as the jury's verdict, and the deck's decision score inherits the same contamination. Because the repo also has no assignments table (claim 4), there is no role recorded on the evaluation either — the only role available is the evaluator's current user role, which nothing in the query consults. I found no meeting note or issue-log entry that chose this behaviour deliberately.
findings.fix: Filter human_avg to jury-lens evaluations (join users and restrict to the edition's jury role — jury for incubator, ic_member for VC), or keep the all-hands average but rename the column and stop using it as the jury aggregate in decisionScore.

findings.screen: buy credits / admin console → Credits & billing
findings.title: No credit_ledger — credits are a bare counter, so per-deck spend, usage history and 'of N purchased' have no backing data
findings.proto: Spec §12 lists `credit_ledger(id, org_id ⟶ organizations, delta int, reason[trial_grant|deck_evaluated|purchase], deck_id ⟶ decks nullable, created_at)`; §13 lists `GET /orgs/:id/credits` → 'balance + ledger'; §10 fixes the metering rule 'one credit per deck evaluated; new orgs start with trial credits (e.g. 3)'. The console section renders it: live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/admin/s-bl.html shows 'Credits remaining 47 of 50 purchased', 'Used this month 3 · ₹2,997 consumed', and a 'Usage history' list of per-deck rows ('GreenGrid Energy — pitchdeck evaluation | 1 credit · ₹999 · 4 Jun 2026') above 'Buy more credits / Download invoice / Upgrade plan'.
findings.repo: `grep -rn credit_ledger` across the repo returns nothing. The entire credit model is one integer: migrations/0001_init.sql:18 `org_settings.credits_balance`. src/server/routes/config.ts:372 POST /credits and :390 POST /credits/purchase both just UPDATE that counter (`credits_balance = credits_balance + ?`), and there is no GET that returns anything but the scalar (config.ts:99 /summary → creditsBalance, config.ts:122 / → creditsBalance). src/client/routes/BuyCreditsPage.tsx has no history, invoice or 'purchased' section — grep for history/transaction/ledger/Recent in it returns nothing. src/server/routes/decks.ts:1169 already reasons about giving a credit back on AI failure ('A terminal failure gave the credit back; re-driving spends it again') but has nowhere to record either event.
findings.gap: Nothing in the product can answer 'which decks consumed my credits, when, and what did I pay'. Without a ledger there is no 'of 50 purchased' denominator, no 'used this month', no per-deck usage rows, no purchase or refund record, and no invoice source — and the refund path in decks.ts:1169 silently mutates a counter with no audit. This is one of §12's 21 tables and one of §13's 14 endpoints, and the auditor's schema and API-surface findings do not mention either.

findings.screen: cross-cutting (every score badge, matrix cell and pipeline bar)
findings.title: Runtime scoring bands are 4 with the wrong cutoffs and wrong labels, not the spec's 5
findings.proto: Spec §1 'Key enums' fixes it: 'Scoring bands (applied per area, 0–10): 9–10 Exceptional · 7–8 Strong · 5–6 Moderate · 3–4 Weak · 0–2 Insufficient.' §7 restates it as a function — 'Band mapping (band(v)): v≥9 → Exceptional(0), v≥7 → Strong(1), v≥5 → Moderate(2), v≥3 → Weak(3), else Insufficient(4). Band index also drives colour coding.' §12's parameter_rubric_bands pins the same five as its band_label enum [9–10|7–8|5–6|3–4|0–2]. The prototype implements it verbatim at AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:3632 `function band(v){ return v>=9?0:v>=7?1:v>=5?2:v>=3?3:4; }`, and admin/s-rb.html calls it 'the BRD five-band scale'.
findings.repo: src/shared/scoring.ts:19-26 `signalTag`: `if (value >= 8) return 'strong'; if (value >= 5) return 'moderate'; if (value >= 2) return 'weak'; return 'absent';` — four bands, different thresholds, and neither 'Exceptional' nor 'Insufficient' exists as a label anywhere (`grep -rni 'exceptional|insufficient' src/` finds nothing). migrations/0002_seed.sql:5-9 seeds rubric_anchors to match: strong 8-10, moderate 5-7, weak 2-4, absent 0-1. The same four-way split is baked into the token names (index.css:28-31 --color-signal-strong/moderate/weak/absent) and into the analytics band accounting (src/shared/analytics.ts:345 'Signal band index … (0=absent … 3=strong)').
findings.gap: Every band chip in the product reports a different band from the one the spec defines: 7.5 is 'Strong' per §1/§7 but renders 'Moderate'; 9.5 is 'Exceptional' but renders 'Strong'; 1.5 is 'Insufficient' but renders 'Absent'. Because §7 says the band index drives colour coding, the colour of every score in every matrix, badge and pipeline bar is off too, and the AI is told the wrong anchors (src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:313-317 builds the band list straight from these four rubric_anchors rows). This is the RUNTIME half of the rubric problem and is separately fixable from the auditor's claim 10, which reports only the missing per-parameter band descriptor STORAGE and mentions the four-band split as an aside without scoring it as a gap.

findings.title: All 9 incubator role parameters are seeded with the wrong names — the spec's canonical set is nowhere in the repo
findings.proto: Spec §1 role-parameter table and §6.2 fix the canonical set: Program Manager = TRL stage · Product-Market Fit · Traction; Program Associate = Program fit · Investment stage · Ask; Jury Member = Barriers of entry · Scalability · Industry growth — each with the exact description and AI prompt printed in §6.2. §6.2 closes with an explicit rule: 'Consistency rule: these role-parameter names are canonical across every file … Keep the standard 13 areas and these 3×3 role parameters identical everywhere.' The live prototype agrees: AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:874 `var ROLE_PARAMS = { pm:[TRL stage, Product-Market Fit, Traction], pa:[Program fit, Investment stage, Ask], jury:[Barriers of entry, Scalability, Industry growth] }`, _scripts.js:3640 CUSTOM_PARAMS repeats the jury three, and panel-myparams.html renders the same nine with their scoring descriptions.
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql seeds nine entirely different names and prompts: program_associate = 'Program & Mandate Fit' / 'Application Readiness' / 'Founder Coachability Signal'; program_manager = 'Program Fit' / 'Mentor Engagement Potential' / 'Cohort Contribution Potential'; jury = 'Founder Resilience & Coachability' / 'Product-Market Fit Signal' / 'Team Execution Capability'. Nine of nine differ. `grep -rn 'TRL' src migrations` returns nothing; so do 'Barriers of entry', 'Industry growth' and 'Investment stage'. These rows are what MyParamsPage.tsx renders, what src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:323 feeds the model, and what EvaluationReport.tsx:237 groups under each role heading.
findings.gap: The three parameters every incubator role actually scores are not the three the spec declares canonical — the labels, the scorer-facing meaning and the AI prompts are all different, on every screen at once (My Parameters, the scoring form, the report's role sections, drift analytics). Spec §11 warns about precisely this trap: it notes the prototype's Team & roles surface 'still carries the old placeholder names (Founder resilience & coachability, etc.); align it if you want full consistency' — the repo shipped those placeholders as the real parameter set instead of the canonical §6.2 names. The auditor's claim 8 covers the missing weight/description FIELDS on this screen but never checks the parameter VALUES.
findings.fix: New migration renaming the nine incubator rows (and replacing their prompts with the §6.2 text verbatim), keeping ids stable so existing scores stay attached; add the §6.2 descriptions once a description column exists. Check the roles harness and any test asserting on the current names.

findings.title: §10's billing-approval chain is entirely absent — tickets have a boolean flag, not an approval workflow
findings.proto: Spec §10 states the requirement in one line: 'Support/ticketing: shared module with Admin and Super User views and a billing-approval chain.' §12 gives it a column: `support_tickets(… status, billing_approval_state)`. The prototype implements the whole chain at AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:4056-4160 — each ticket carries `billing:{kind:'credits'|'seats', qty, tier, cost, ctx}` and `approval ∈ none|pending|approved|declined`, plus a message thread; the actions are tkRequestApproval ('Request Super User approval'), the Super User's approve / tkDecline ('Declined for now — please reassign an existing seat…'), and tkFulfil ('Fulfil & resolve'); the queue has an 'Awaiting approval (n)' filter chip (:4098, counted by tkCounts :4078) and a pending badge 'Awaiting approval' (:4082-4086); the read-only role variant retitles the screen 'Read-only overview — plus approvals for seat & credit requests routed to you' (:4092).
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:185-194 gives tickets only `billing_routed INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`; no approval column is ever added (0018 adds category/severity/area/assignee_id/resolution/updated_at only). src/server/routes/support.ts:67-69 sets billing_routed automatically from a regex on the subject/body (`/\b(billing|credit|invoice|payment|refund)\b/i`) — nobody routes anything. The only mutation route is support.ts:81 POST /:id/status, which accepts 'closed' or 'open' and nothing else. There is no ticket-message/thread table and no reply route (`grep -n 'thread|reply|ticket_messages' src/server/routes/support.ts` is empty). src/client/routes/SupportPages.tsx:116 renders a static `Billing`/`General` badge and no approval controls.
findings.gap: A seat or credit request — the thing the chain exists for — cannot be raised with its qty/tier/cost payload, cannot be routed to the Super User, cannot be approved, declined or fulfilled, and has no conversation thread; the queue has no 'Awaiting approval' state to filter on and no Super-User-vs-Admin view split. Ticket status is a two-value open/closed against the prototype's open / in progress / resolved / overdue. §10 is one of the five cross-cutting behaviours in this lane and the auditor reported none of it.

findings.title: All nine VC role-specific parameter names differ from the canonical set
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §6.2 + §10; live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:2047 `var JP_ADDL={jp:['Thesis fit','Investment stage','Ask / Ticket size fit'],pp:['TRL stage','Product-Market Fit','Traction']}`; panel-myparams.html carries all nine incl. Barriers of entry / Scalability / Exit attractiveness
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:47-66 — associate: Thesis & Mandate Fit, Deal Readiness, Founder Conviction Signal; partner: Ownership & Return Math, Portfolio Construction Fit, Conviction to Sponsor; ic_member: Founder Resilience & Coachability, Product-Market Fit Signal, Team Execution Capability
findings.gap: Nine of nine names are wrong, and the one near-match (Product-Market Fit) is assigned to the wrong role — the spec puts it on Partner, the repo on IC Member. §11 gotcha 7 makes these names canonical across every surface.
findings.fix: Rename the nine rows (and their prompts/descriptions) to the canonical set in a new migration; keep the ids so existing scores stay attached.

findings.title: Parameter editor is missing the weight select, the scorer-facing description, Reset and Save all
findings.proto: panel-myparams.html — per parameter: "Parameter label", "Scoring weight in their composite" (Informational (not weighted) / 5% additional weight / 10% additional weight), "Description shown to user during scoring", "AI extraction prompt for this parameter" with a Reset button; panel header carries "Save all"
findings.repo: src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:145-235 — label + AI prompt only; src/server/routes/config.ts:274 accepts only { name, prompt }; migrations/0001_init.sql:30 `parameters` has no description column; config.ts:169 rejects any weight edit on an informational param (`invalid_param`)
findings.gap: Role parameters can never be raised from Informational to 5%/10% as §6.2/§12 require, and the description the scorer reads during evaluation has nowhere to live.
findings.fix: Add `parameters.description`; allow weight ∈ {0, 5, 10} on informational params through a dedicated endpoint; add the select, description textarea, Reset-to-default and Save all to MyParamsPage.

findings.title: No "Configure 3 additional parameters" grant; Partners cannot edit
findings.proto: panel-myparams.html — "Super Users, Partners and Client Admins can edit by default. Other roles are read-only here unless granted the 'Configure 3 additional parameters' permission in Admin → Team & roles", plus the mp-grant toggle and mpApplyPerm() at _scripts.js:4028-4053; live/specs/vc.html §10 and §12 `user_roles.can_configure_params`
findings.repo: src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:32 `const canEdit = user?.role === "admin" || user?.role === "superuser";`; src/server/routes/config.ts:215/261/291 all requireRole("admin"); no can_configure_params column anywhere in migrations/
findings.gap: Partners are read-only against the spec, and the per-user grant that Admin → Team & roles is supposed to hand out does not exist in schema, API or UI.
findings.fix: Add users.can_configure_params (or a user_roles row), surface the toggle in the Admin console Team & roles editor, include partner in the default editors, and check the flag in MyParamsPage plus the three config endpoints.

findings.title: AI does not pre-fill the human score
findings.proto: spec §10 'AI pre-fills a suggested score using each parameter's prompt'; panel-myparams.html 'The AI pre-populates a suggested score for their custom parameters just as it does for the 13 standard areas. The user can override.'
findings.repo: src/client/routes/EvaluatePage.tsx:107 `setValues(Object.fromEntries(allScored.map((p) => [p.key, 5])))` — every parameter starts at a flat 5; the AI value is fetched into `aiScores` (EvaluatePage.tsx:87-95) but only rendered for reference (EvaluatePage.tsx:478)
findings.gap: The evaluator starts from 5 on all 22 parameters instead of from the AI suggestion, so 'override' is not what the user does, and there is no `overridden` flag to distinguish an accepted AI score from a deliberate human one (spec §12 evaluation_scores.overridden).
findings.fix: Seed `values` from the loaded AI scores per parameter key, fall back to 5 only when the AI has no value, and record overridden when the human changes it.

findings.title: Parameter configuration is admin-only; PM / Client Admin default and the per-user grant are missing
findings.proto: spec §10 'parameter configuration is editable by Super Users, Program Managers and Client Admins by default; other roles are read-only unless granted "Configure 3 additional parameters" in Admin → Team & roles'; panel-myparams.html permission card + 'Previewing as' role switcher (Super User · Client Admin · Program Manager · Program Associate · Jury Member) + 'Permission granted' toggle + read-only banner
findings.repo: src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:32 `const canEdit = user?.role === "admin" || user?.role === "superuser"`; every config route is `requireRole("admin")` (config.ts:151, 215, 261, 291); nav.ts:105 gates `coreparams` to `roles: ["admin"]`; no `can_configure_params` column exists (grep across src/ + migrations/ returns nothing)
findings.gap: A Program Manager cannot edit any parameter, contradicting the spec default and the PM prototype sidebar which carries Core Parameters. There is no grant mechanism at all, so no role can ever be raised to editable, and the permission card / role preview / read-only banner are absent from the screen.
findings.fix: Add user_roles.can_configure_params, treat super_user + program_manager + admin as editable by default, honour the grant elsewhere, and build the permission card.

findings.title: Ticketing has no billing-approval chain, no thread and no billing payload
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §10 — "a billing-approval chain"; _scripts.js — `t.billing && t.approval==='approved'|'declined'|'pending'`, `billing:{kind:'seats'|'credits', qty, tier, cost, ctx}`, thread pushes ("…billing for approval, resolve"), provisioning on approval ("50 credits added"); panel-support.html columns ID · Ticket · Category · Priority · Status · Age with four stat tiles and filter chips
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:185 `tickets(… status, billing_routed …)` + ALTERs adding category/severity/area/assignee/resolution; src/server/routes/support.ts:62-92 — POST sets a boolean billing_routed by keyword match, POST /:id/status flips open|closed only
findings.gap: billing_routed is a routing hint with no approver, no approve/decline decision, no seat/credit request payload, no conversation thread and no provisioning action, so an approved credit request cannot actually add credits.
findings.fix: Add billing_approval_state plus a billing payload (kind, qty, tier, cost, context) and a ticket_messages thread; add approve/decline endpoints that credit the balance or add seats on approval.

findings.title: Report is per-evaluator columns, not stage-detected role sections
findings.proto: spec §11 'Report role sections are stage-detected via visible panel'; §8.4 Assign stage → PA + PM sections, Intro calls stage → PA + PM + Jury (jury read-only 'completed'), other stages → single-role; Jury file: Assigned adds a PA reference section, Intro calls adds PA + PM. Spec §13 `GET /decks/:id/report?stage=assign|intro`
findings.repo: src/server/routes/decks.ts:634 `decks.get("/:id/report")` reads no query parameter; the payload is built as one Column per evaluator (decks.ts:698 'Evaluators are sourced from BOTH the roll-up and the per-parameter scores'); src/client/components/EvaluationReport.tsx:167 'One column per evaluator — the report widens as the deck passes hands'; `grep 'stage=' src/client/api.ts` returns nothing
findings.gap: The report shape is evaluator-driven rather than stage-driven, so it never renders the named 'Program associate' / 'Program manager' / 'Jury' parameter sections, never marks the jury section read-only-completed at the intro stage, and cannot be opened in a different shape from Assign vs Intro calls.
findings.fix: Accept ?stage=assign|intro, group rows into role sections per §8.4, and mark completed sections read-only.

findings.title: No credit ledger: credits are one mutable integer with no history of trial grants, per-deck consumption or purchases
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §12 `credit_ledger ( id, fund_id ⟶ funds, delta int, reason[ trial_grant | deck_evaluated | purchase ], deck_id ⟶ decks nullable, created_at )`; §13 `GET /funds/:id/credits balance + ledger`; §10 "Evaluation is credit-metered — one credit per deck evaluated; new funds start with trial credits on Standard."
findings.repo: `grep -rn "credit_ledger|ledger" src/ migrations/` returns no schema hit (only unrelated seed prose). The entire model is `org_settings.credits_balance INTEGER` (migrations/0001_init.sql:21). src/server/routes/config.ts:372-381 POST /credits OVERWRITES the balance with an absolute number; :390-409 POST /credits/purchase does an atomic `credits_balance = credits_balance + ?` and returns only the new balance. No GET returns a ledger — config.ts:99-118 and :122-138 expose `creditsBalance` alone. src/client/routes/BuyCreditsPage.tsx contains no history/ledger/transaction rendering.
findings.gap: There is no audit trail for credits at all: nobody can answer "which decks consumed our credits", "when did this top-up land", or "was this a trial grant". Because POST /config/credits replaces rather than deltas, an admin adjustment silently destroys the prior balance with no record. This blocks the §13 credits endpoint outright and leaves the Credits & billing surfaces with a bare number. Flagging it here because it is a §12/§13 table+endpoint pair in this lane; the admin-console Credits & billing section belongs to the other lane and will need the same table.

findings.title: No per-parameter rubric bands — one global 4-band table instead of 5 bands per area
findings.proto: spec §12 `parameter_rubric_bands(id, parameter_id, band_label[9–10|7–8|5–6|3–4|0–2], band_index, description)`; §7 'Rubric text per band exists per area (5 short descriptors guiding the scorer)'; §7 band(v): ≥9 Exceptional, ≥7 Strong, ≥5 Moderate, ≥3 Weak, else Insufficient. AISJ_IC_SuserV15/admin/s-rb.html 'Rubric anchors … define what each score band means on the BRD five-band scale (0–2 · 3–4 · 5–6 · 7–8 · 9–10)' with a per-area/per-parameter selector; _scripts.js `function band(v){return v>=9?0:v>=7?1:v>=5?2:v>=3?3:4}` and `evParams[i].rubric[bi].desc` used for the report's remark column
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:44 `rubric_anchors(band, min_score, max_score, label)` — a single global table; migrations/0002_seed.sql:5 seeds four rows (strong 8-10, moderate 5-7, weak 2-4, absent 0-1) with a one-word label each; src/shared/scoring.ts:21-26 `signalTag` is the matching 4-way split
findings.gap: There is nowhere to store the 13 areas × 5 band descriptors the scorer reads, and the report cannot fill its rubric-remark column. Note the prototype carries two band systems — the 5-band BRD rubric (admin s-rb, band()) and the 4-band signal classification (panel-settings) — and the repo implements only the latter; the 5-band per-parameter rubric text is the missing one.
findings.fix: Add parameter_rubric_bands keyed to parameter_definitions with band_index 0-4 and description; keep the 4-band signal tag as a separate display concept.

findings.title: Term sheet has no signing model: no signatory, provider, signature type or in-app/wet-ink flags
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §8.3 — "an authorised signatory is assigned in-workspace before countersign; a signing method is chosen per record and locked once signed", provider ∈ {SignDesk, DocuSign, Adobe, Zoho, eMudhra}, sigType ∈ {Standard e-signature, Certificate (DSC/Aadhaar/QES)}, flags inApp / wetInk
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:162 `term_sheets(id, deck_id, valuation, ownership, notes, created_at)`; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:134 inserts it as a side effect of the issue_term_sheet transition
findings.gap: No status, no provider, no signature type, no authorised signatory and no lock-once-signed rule; the Term sheet Pipeline screen therefore cannot show or drive the signing state.
findings.fix: Extend term_sheets with status, signing_provider, sig_type, in_app, wet_ink, authorised_signatory_user_id; add POST /decks/:id/term-sheet and a PATCH that refuses changes after signing.

findings.title: No diligence item model: Investment DD and Legal DD are deck lists, not document checklists
findings.proto: _scripts.js:1381-1383 `DD_ITEMS = ['Market','Team references','Customer calls','Product / Tech review','Financials & metrics','Competitive positioning']`, DD_STATUSES, DD_RATINGS; :1733 `LD_ITEMS = ['Cap table verification','IP assignment','Contracts & customer agreements','Employment / ESOP','Regulatory / compliance','Litigation checks','Legal documentation (SHA / SSA)']`; ddRender() renders an "Open checklist" button, progress and flagged count per deal; suVerifyAll() is the "Verify all documents" bulk action
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:144 `investment_dd(id, deck_id, notes, mp_approved)` and :171 `legal_dd(id, deck_id, notes)` — one notes row per deck; src/client/routes/StagePage.tsx:617/636 render both slugs as plain deck tables; grep for not_requested / "Verify all" across src/ returns nothing
findings.gap: The four-state per-item flow (not_requested → awaiting → submitted → verified), the item lists, the per-deal progress/flag rollup and the Verify-all bulk action are all absent.
findings.fix: Add diligence_items(deck_id, track, name, status, file_url, verified_by) seeded with the two item lists, a PATCH route per item, a bulk verify, and a checklist drawer on both screens.

findings.title: Capital deployment is never recorded; the Capital report runs on seed data only
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §8.3.3 — "record the deployment against the fund's committed capital (the 'Fund Deployment' surface that replaces the incubator's 'Seat capacity')"; §12 capital_deployments(id, deck_id, amount, deployed_at, recorded_by); §13 POST /decks/:id/deploy
findings.repo: src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:146-151 — complete_legal_dd inserts `portfolio(id, deck_id, onboarded_at)` with no amount; migrations/0001_init.sql:178 `portfolio(… capital_deployed TEXT …)` is written only by migrations/0008_seed_analytics.sql:103; src/server/routes/analytics.ts:205 reads it
findings.gap: There is no route, screen or field that sets capital_deployed, so "Capital Deployment & Pacing" and "Portfolio Construction" show seeded numbers that can never change in production. There is also no `deployed` pipeline state.
findings.fix: Add capital_deployments plus POST /decks/:id/deploy (amount, date, recorder), a deploy step on the Onboard-ready/Capital screen, and a `deployed` stage between legal_dd and onboard_ready.

findings.title: Rubric bands are a single global 4-band table on the wrong thresholds, not 5 bands per parameter
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §7 `band(v): v≥9 Exceptional, v≥7 Strong, v≥5 Moderate, v≥3 Weak, else Insufficient` — confirmed in _scripts.js:4136 `function band(v){ return v>=9?0:v>=7?1:v>=5?2:v>=3?3:4; }` and the founder-portal legend (_rest.html:1495 "9–10 Exceptional — fully evidenced & verified"); §12 parameter_rubric_bands(parameter_id, band_label, band_index, description)
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:44 `rubric_anchors(band PRIMARY KEY, min_score, max_score, label)` — one global row set; migrations/0002_seed.sql:5-9 seeds four bands at 8/5/2/0; src/shared/scoring.ts:21-26 `signalTag` uses ≥8 / ≥5 / ≥2
findings.gap: Band count, thresholds, labels and per-parameter scoping are all wrong, so every colour chip and signal pill buckets scores differently from the prototype. The correct five bands exist only in one analytics helper (src/shared/analytics.ts:181-187, which itself says "0–2 Absent" instead of "Insufficient").
findings.fix: Add parameter_rubric_bands keyed by parameter with the five spec bands and descriptions; re-point signalTag and the pill styles at 9/7/5/3; rename Absent → Insufficient.

findings.title: No assignments table: one assignee per deck, with no role or stage
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §5 "Deck ∞───∞ User via Assignment (deck ↔ evaluator, carries role + stage)" and §12 assignments(id, deck_id, user_id, role, stage, assigned_by, assigned_at); panel-assign.html assigns one deck to MULTIPLE members of a role
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:52 `decks.assigned_to TEXT REFERENCES users(id)` — a single column; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:296 overwrites it on each assign
findings.gap: A deck can be assigned to exactly one evaluator at a time, the assignment carries no stage, and the prototype's multi-member confirm loop (which writes one row per deck×member) has nowhere to persist.
findings.fix: Add the assignments table and read the evaluator set from it; keep decks.assigned_to only as a denormalised convenience if needed.

findings.title: No pending → draft → submitted lifecycle: evaluations are single-shot and not per-stage
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §8.1 and §12 `evaluations(… role, stage, state[pending|draft|submitted] …)`; §13 POST /decks/:id/evaluations, PATCH /evaluations/:id, POST /evaluations/:id/submit
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:98 `evaluations(id, deck_id, evaluator_id, weighted_total, verdict, remarks, submitted_at)` — no state, role or stage column; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:400 inserts with verdict 'scored' in one shot; no draft endpoint and no client-side draft (grep for saveDraft/Save draft in src/ returns nothing)
findings.gap: An evaluator cannot save partial work, and the same evaluator scoring the same deck at two different gates collapses into one row, which also breaks the per-stage committee aggregation in §12's views.
findings.fix: Add state/role/stage to evaluations with a unique key on (deck, evaluator, stage); add the open/draft/submit endpoints; block submit until every applicable parameter is scored.

findings.title: No evaluation draft lifecycle — pending / draft / submitted endpoints absent
findings.proto: spec §13 `POST /decks/:id/evaluations` (open pending), `PATCH /evaluations/:id` (save draft), `POST /evaluations/:id/submit` (validate all-scored → submitted); §8.1 pending → draft → submitted, submission blocked until every applicable parameter is scored
findings.repo: src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:322 POST /api/decks/:id/evaluate is the only write path — it deletes prior rows and inserts `evaluations(... verdict 'scored', submitted_at)` in one shot (pipeline.ts:396-400); it rejects only when zero scores arrive (pipeline.ts:374 `if (clean.length === 0)`); unscored parameters silently count 0 (pipeline.ts:378-380). `grep -rn draft src/server/` matches only calls.ts:398
findings.gap: No pending row, no draft persistence, no all-scored submit gate. An evaluator who scores 3 of 22 parameters produces a `submitted` evaluation whose composite treats the other 19 as zero, and the jury 'Drafts' count the prototype shows has no backing state.
findings.fix: Add evaluations.state + updated_at, the three endpoints, and an all-applicable-parameters-scored check on submit.

findings.title: Sign-up document and signature endpoints absent
findings.proto: spec §13 `PATCH /signups/:id/documents/:docId` set document status, `POST /agreements/:id/sign` record signature; §8.3 per-document status ladder with 'Verify all', agreements library, signing method locked once the founder signs
findings.repo: No such routes in src/server/index.ts or src/server/routes/*.ts. The nearest are decks.ts:424 `PUT /api/decks/:id/onboarding` (one `documentsStatus` enum for the whole deck, decks.ts:454) and pipeline.ts:602 `POST /api/decks/:id/send-signup`
findings.gap: Nothing at all — no route and no table (see the sign-up schema finding). Documents can only be flagged wholesale, and a signature cannot be recorded.
findings.fix: Add the two endpoints on top of signup_documents / agreements / signatures.

findings.screen: §14 Brand Tokens (global chrome — Topbar, Sidebar, Button, index.css)
findings.title: The olive brand family is absent from the design tokens — the app is amber-accented where the prototype is olive-accented
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §14 lists the palette olive-first: "Olive #6B8454 · Olive-dark #4A6644 / #4A5E3A · Military green #3B4A3F · Amber/gold #E8A020 · Gold-dark #B87A10 · Off-white #F5F7F2 · Stone-dark #D4D0C8". live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_style.css declares --olive:#6B8454, --olive-lt:#EBF0E4, --olive-md:#8FA67A, --olive-dk:#4A5E3A, --stone:#ECEAE4, --stone-dk:#D4D0C8, --gold:#E8A020, --gold-dk:#B87A10 and uses them: `.an{…background:var(--olive-dk)…}` (top nav), `.si.on{background:var(--olive-lt);color:var(--olive-dk);border-left-color:var(--olive)}` (active sidebar item), `.btn-primary{…background:var(--gold-dk);color:#fff…}`, `.as-chk.on{background:var(--olive);border-color:var(--olive)}`. Usage counts in that one stylesheet: var(--olive) 83, --olive-dk 95, --olive-lt 54, --stone-dk 173 vs --gold 20, --gold-lt 18 — olive is the primary identity, gold the highlight.
findings.repo: src/client/index.css:16-20 @theme defines only --color-amber #e8a020, --color-navy, --color-offwhite #f5f7f2, --color-military #3b4a3f, --color-deepgreen #4a6644; :49 --topbar: #3b4a3f; :53 --sidebar-active: #fdf3e0 (the prototype's --gold-lt); :54 --accent: #e8a020. src/client/components/Button.tsx:7-8 primary = "bg-amber text-navy". src/client/components/Sidebar.tsx:94 active = "bg-sidebar-active … ring-1 ring-amber/25". `grep -rni "6b8454|4a5e3a|b87a10|d4d0c8|ebf0e4|8fa67a|ecead4" src/` returns ZERO hits.
findings.gap: Four of the eight tokens the spec names have no value in the repo (#6B8454, #4A5E3A, #B87A10, #D4D0C8), and the accent role is inverted: the prototype's primary button is gold-dark #B87A10 on white while the repo's is amber #E8A020 on navy; the prototype's active sidebar row is olive-tinted with an olive left border while the repo's is gold-tinted with an amber ring; the prototype's top nav is olive-dark #4A5E3A while the repo's is military green #3B4A3F. Since the client's brief is "exactly match the way it should look", this is the single largest look-and-feel divergence in this lane and it is systemic — it changes every screen at once. Logo (radar mark, src/client/components/Logo.tsx) and the tagline default (ConfigPage.tsx:391 "Venture Intelligence First") are correct; only the palette is wrong.

findings.title: Eight palette tokens have no counterpart in the repo
findings.proto: AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js `brBrandTokens` / `brStatusTokens`: --olive Primary #6B8454 (82 uses in _style.css), --olive-lt Primary light #EBF0E4 (50), --olive-md Primary muted #8FA67A, --gold-dk Accent dark #B87A10 (74), --stone Surface / soft border #ECEAE4 (100), --stone-dk Border #D4D0C8 (166), --text-2 Text secondary #4A4840 (62), --purple Special #7C3AED. Spec §14 names Olive #6B8454, Gold-dark #B87A10 and Stone-dark #D4D0C8 explicitly
findings.repo: src/client/index.css:11-36 (@theme) and 40-73 (:root) define no equivalent; `grep -ril '6B8454|4A5E3A|B87A10|D4D0C8|ECEAE4' src/` returns nothing
findings.gap: The primary olive ramp, the accent-dark, the two stone neutrals, the secondary text colour and the 'Special' purple simply do not exist in the implementation, so any screen the prototype paints with them renders in a substituted colour.
findings.fix: Add all 18 tokens as :root custom properties and map them into the Tailwind theme.

findings.title: Credits are a bare balance with no ledger
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #5 — `Organization 1───1 Subscription ───(plan tier) 1───∞ CreditLedgerEntry`; #12 `credit_ledger(org_id, delta, reason[trial_grant|deck_evaluated|purchase], deck_id, created_at)`
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:21 `credits_balance INTEGER` on org_settings is the only credit state; grep `credit_ledger|ledger` across migrations/ and src/ returns no table (only unrelated seed prose). No `subscriptions` table either — plan lives as `org_settings.plan` with no status or renews_at.
findings.gap: There is no per-deck record of which evaluation consumed which credit, no purchase history and no trial grant, so the credits screen cannot show a statement and a disputed charge cannot be traced.
findings.fix: Add credit_ledger and subscriptions; write a ledger row on trial grant, deck evaluation and purchase, and derive the balance.

findings.title: Evaluation carries no stage — a later gate overwrites the earlier one
findings.proto: Spec §5: "Evaluation is one person's scoring of one deck at one stage-gate"; §7: "Committee aggregation: across all evaluations of a deck AT A GATE, average the per-parameter scores and the composite." The prototype reports per gate (_scripts.js:4229-4310 builds a distinct column set for analystScored / introScored / partnerScored / pcScored).
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql `evaluations` has no stage column; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:390 `DELETE FROM evaluations WHERE deck_id = ? AND evaluator_id = ?` before every insert; src/server/routes/decks.ts:58 `human_avg` = `AVG(e.weighted_total) … WHERE e.deck_id = d.id` with no gate filter.
findings.gap: A partner who scores at partner_review and again at a later gate loses the first record, and every aggregate blends all gates together. The per-gate report columns the prototype builds cannot be reconstructed from this schema.
findings.fix: Add `evaluations.stage` (and the same on `scores`), key the idempotent replace on (deck, evaluator, stage), and filter aggregates by stage where §7 says 'at a gate'.

findings.title: The 13 standard areas have no per-area AI extraction prompt
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #61 — "Each area also has an AI extraction prompt (per-area; prototype stores these per org)"; #2 — "the platform's AI pre-populates a suggested score … using per-parameter extraction prompts"; admin/s-rb.html — "For each area or parameter, write an AI guidance prompt (what the AI should look for)"
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:16-18 — "NULL for core areas, which fall back to name + weight". src/server/ai/evaluate.ts:323 `const guidance = p.prompt ? substituteVars(p.prompt, ctx) : \`Score ${p.name} 0–10.\`` — the core-13 branch is the bare fallback. Only `org_settings.ai_system_prompt` (migrations/0001_init.sql:22) is org-configurable.
findings.gap: Twelve of the thirteen areas are scored by the model on their name alone. The per-area guidance prompt the admin console's Rubric anchors section is designed to author has nowhere to live.
findings.fix: Populate `parameters.prompt` for the core 13, seed sensible defaults, and expose them in the Rubric anchors section alongside the band descriptors.

findings.title: Four global rubric anchors instead of five per-parameter bands with descriptions
findings.proto: Spec §5 "ParameterDefinition 1───∞ ParameterRubricBand (5 bands per standard area)"; §7 `band(v)`: ≥9 Exceptional, ≥7 Strong, ≥5 Moderate, ≥3 Weak, else Insufficient. live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:4136 `function band(v){return v>=9?0:v>=7?1:v>=5?2:v>=3?3:4}`; :440 each of the 13 areas carries `rubric:[{band:'9–10',desc:…},{'7–8'},{'5–6'},{'3–4'},{'0–2'}]` plus five `criteria` clarification questions and its own `prompt`.
findings.repo: migrations/0002_seed.sql:5-9 `rubric_anchors` is a FOUR-row global table (strong 8-10, moderate 5-7, weak 2-4, absent 0-1); src/shared/scoring.ts:21 `signalTag` uses the same 8/5/2 cut-points; the `rubric_anchors` table is keyed by band, not by parameter. Only src/shared/analytics.ts:182-186 carries the correct five bands (and labels the last '0–2 Absent' rather than 'Insufficient').
findings.gap: Band boundaries, band count, band labels and colour coding all differ from the spec, and there are no per-area anchor descriptions — so the report's AI-remark expander (which shows `p.rubric[band(v)].desc`) has no data source.
findings.fix: Replace the global table with `parameter_rubric_bands(parameter_id, band_index, min, max, label, description)` seeded with the prototype's five bands per area; re-point signalTag/scoreColor at the 9/7/5/3 cut-points and the Exceptional…Insufficient labels.

findings.title: Only admin/superuser can configure parameters; the PM is locked out and there is no per-user grant
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #10 — "parameter configuration is editable by Super Users, Program Managers and Client Admins by default; other roles are read-only unless granted 'Configure 3 additional parameters' in Admin → Team & roles"; panel-myparams.html carries that exact copy plus a "Permission granted" toggle and the read-only message
findings.repo: src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:32 `const canEdit = user?.role === "admin" || user?.role === "superuser"`. src/server/routes/config.ts:215, 261 both `requireRole("admin")`. No `can_configure_params` column anywhere (grep across migrations/ and src/shared/ → zero hits).
findings.gap: A Program Manager — one of the three default editors — gets a read-only screen with no explanation, and the "Configure 3 additional parameters" grant has no column, no admin control and no check. The repo also hides the whole screen behind an EmptyState on non-Premium plans where the prototype shows it read-only with a plan explanation (MyParamsPage.tsx:76-83 vs AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:3495).
findings.fix: Add `users.can_configure_params`, admit program_manager by default, grant/revoke it in Admin → Team & roles, and render read-only-with-reason instead of hiding.

findings.title: Additional parameters have no weight option and no scorer-facing description
findings.proto: Spec §5: "A parameter has: name, scope, weight, description-shown-to-scorer, AI-extraction prompt"; §6.2: "Default weight Informational (not weighted into the composite unless the fund raises it to 5% / 10%)". live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/panel-myparams.html — every parameter card has 'Parameter label', a 'Scoring weight in their composite' select (Informational (not weighted) / 5% additional weight / 10% additional weight), 'Description shown to user during scoring' and 'AI extraction prompt … Reset'.
findings.repo: src/server/routes/config.ts:274-286 `PUT /additional-params/:id` accepts only `name` and `prompt`; :246 the INSERT hard-codes weight 0 and informational 1; migrations/0001_init.sql `parameters` has no description column.
findings.gap: A fund can never raise a role parameter to 5% or 10%, and the description the spec says is 'visible to them during scoring' has nowhere to live — so the scoring UI shows a bare label.
findings.fix: Add `parameters.description`; allow weight ∈ {0, 5, 10} on additional params via the config PUT (weight > 0 must then be folded into the composite denominator in weightedTotal); surface both in MyParamsPage and in the scorecard.

findings.title: All nine role parameters carry the stale placeholder names, not the canonical set
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #62-role-specific-parameters-3-per-role (PM: TRL stage / Product-Market Fit / Traction · PA: Program fit / Investment stage / Ask · Jury: Barriers of entry / Scalability / Industry growth); confirmed verbatim in live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/panel-myparams.html (rp-pm / rp-pa / rp-men) and in AISJ_IC_Jury_V4/_scripts.js:3376-3388 `ROLES={pa:…,pm:…}`. §11 explicitly names "Founder resilience & coachability" as the OLD placeholder to be aligned away.
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:26-49 seeds `Program & Mandate Fit` / `Application Readiness` / `Founder Coachability Signal` (PA), `Program Fit` / `Mentor Engagement Potential` / `Cohort Contribution Potential` (PM), `Founder Resilience & Coachability` / `Product-Market Fit Signal` / `Team Execution Capability` (jury).
findings.gap: Nine of nine incubator role parameters are wrong. The owner roles are correct, so this is a data/label fix rather than a structural one — but §6.2 calls these names canonical across every file, and the prototype scoring views, the jury reference sections and the reports all render them.
findings.fix: Re-seed the nine parameters with the spec's names, descriptions and AI prompts; migrate existing scores by key.

findings.title: The Informational / 5% / 10% weight selector is hardcoded to 0
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #62 — "Default weight Informational (not weighted) … unless the org raises it to 5% / 10%"; panel-myparams.html renders "Scoring weight in their composite: Informational (not weighted) · 5% additional weight · 10% additional weight" per parameter
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:26 inserts every additional param with `weight 0, informational 1`; src/server/routes/config.ts:246 hardcodes `VALUES (…, 0, 1, …)` on create and config.ts:261-270 lets PUT change only name and prompt. src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:197 renders a fixed `<Badge>Informational · assistive</Badge>`.
findings.gap: A role parameter can never be raised to 5% or 10%, so §7's "excluded from the composite unless weighted" branch is unreachable and the selector has no UI.
findings.fix: Allow weight ∈ {0, 5, 10} on additional params, expose the three-way selector, and fold non-zero weights into the composite.

findings.title: "Description shown during scoring" has no column and no field
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #62 — each role parameter has "a scorer-facing description and an AI prompt", with the full text given per parameter; panel-myparams.html labels the textarea "Description shown to user during scoring"; AISJ_IC_Jury_V4/_scripts.js:3378-3387 renders that description under each parameter name in the reference sections
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:29-39 `parameters` has id, edition, key, name, weight, informational, role_scope, sort_order, active; migrations/0013:18 adds only `prompt`. No `description` column exists (grep `ALTER TABLE parameters` → one hit). src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:157 edits name + prompt only.
findings.gap: The scorer-facing description — which the spec supplies verbatim for all nine role parameters and which the prototype shows in both the scoring view and the jury reference sections — cannot be stored, edited or displayed.
findings.fix: Add `parameters.description`, seed it from §6.2, edit it in My Parameters, and render it under the parameter name in the scoring view and report.

findings.title: 8 of 9 VC role-parameter names are invented, not the canonical set
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:2047 `var JP_ADDL={jp:['Thesis fit','Investment stage','Ask / Ticket size fit'],pp:['TRL stage','Product-Market Fit','Traction']}`; :4842 `VC_ROLE_ADDL` (jury→['Barriers of entry','Scalability','Exit attractiveness']); panel-myparams.html renders the same three tabs with label + scoring description + AI prompt each. Spec §6.2: "Consistency rule: these role-parameter names are canonical across every file."
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:47 associate = Thesis & Mandate Fit / Deal Readiness / Founder Conviction Signal; :54 partner = Ownership & Return Math / Portfolio Construction Fit / Conviction to Sponsor; :61 ic_member = Founder Resilience & Coachability / Product-Market Fit Signal / Team Execution Capability
findings.gap: Only 'Thesis fit' loosely survives. The other eight names, and all nine scorer-facing descriptions and AI prompts, are repo inventions. Every report chip, matrix column and My Parameters tab therefore shows the wrong labels.
findings.fix: Re-seed the nine vc role-scoped rows with the canonical names, the §6.2 descriptions and the prototype's AI prompts (panel-myparams.html carries all three verbatim per parameter). Soft-retire the current rows so historical scores stay referenced.

findings.title: Partners cannot configure parameters and the grantable permission does not exist
findings.proto: Spec §10: "parameter configuration is editable by Super Users, Partners and Fund Admins by default; other roles are read-only unless granted 'Configure 3 additional parameters' in Admin → Team & roles." live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/panel-myparams.html — 'Permission to configure additional parameters … Super Users, Partners and Client Admins can edit by default', with a 'Previewing as' row (Super User / Client Admin / Partner / Analyst / IC Member) and a read-only banner for ungranted roles.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:32 `const canEdit = user?.role === "admin" || user?.role === "superuser"`; src/server/routes/config.ts:215, :261, :291 all `requireRole("admin")`.
findings.gap: Partners get a read-only My Parameters screen contrary to the default the spec states, and there is no per-user grant flag at all — so no role can ever be promoted to configure its own three parameters.
findings.fix: Add `partner` to the default editors on both client and server, and add a per-user `can_configure_params` grant (set in Admin → Team & roles) that the config routes honour alongside the role check.

findings.title: Rubric anchors are one global 4-row table, not five bands per area
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #7 — "Rubric text per band exists per area (5 short descriptors guiding the scorer). Store as ParameterRubricBand(parameter_id, band_label, description)"; live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/admin/s-rb.html offers an Evaluation-area picker (01–13 plus the three configurable parameters) and a per-area five-band anchor editor with Save anchors / Revert
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:43-48 `CREATE TABLE rubric_anchors (band TEXT PRIMARY KEY, min_score, max_score, label)` — global, four rows, no parameter_id and no description. src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:944-953 serves those same four rows to every parameter's detail panel.
findings.gap: Every one of the 13 areas shows the same generic band text. The per-area descriptors the scorer is meant to read (and the AI is meant to score against) cannot be stored or edited.
findings.fix: Add `parameter_rubric_bands(parameter_id, band_label, band_index, description)` with 5 rows per parameter, and expose the per-area anchor editor.

findings.title: Scoring bands are four with wrong thresholds and wrong labels
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #1 "9–10 Exceptional · 7–8 Strong · 5–6 Moderate · 3–4 Weak · 0–2 Insufficient" and #7 `band(v)`: v≥9→Exceptional(0), v≥7→Strong(1), v≥5→Moderate(2), v≥3→Weak(3), else Insufficient(4); live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/admin/s-rb.html — "BRD five-band scale (0–2 · 3–4 · 5–6 · 7–8 · 9–10)"
findings.repo: src/shared/scoring.ts:21-27 `signalTag`: >=8 strong, >=5 moderate, >=2 weak, else absent. migrations/0002_seed.sql:5-9 `rubric_anchors` = strong 8-10 / moderate 5-7 / weak 2-4 / absent 0-1. Same four-band thresholds hardcoded again in src/client/components/EvaluationReport.tsx:25-29 and EvalScorecard.tsx `scoreColor`.
findings.gap: Four bands instead of five; every threshold differs (a 7.5 is "Strong" per spec, "moderate" per repo); labels differ (Exceptional/Insufficient vs strong/absent). The band index drives colour coding across the report, chips and pipeline pills, so the whole product colours scores by the wrong rule.
findings.fix: Replace signalTag with the five-band `band(v)`, reseed rubric_anchors to the five BRD bands, and derive every scoreColor from the shared function.

findings.title: No draft state and no completeness gate — every save is a submit, and sliders pre-fill to 5
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:4436 renders both `Save draft` and `Submit my evaluation`; :4501 `jrSubmit` refuses with 'Score all N parameters before submitting (x/N)' until every parameter is scored. Spec §8.1: "pending → draft → submitted. Submission is blocked until every applicable parameter has a score."
findings.repo: src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:337 a single 'Save scores' button; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:400 every save writes `verdict='scored'` with `submitted_at` set; src/client/routes/VcEvaluatePage.tsx:92 `setValues(Object.fromEntries(allScored.map((p) => [p.key, 5])))` pre-fills every parameter to 5.
findings.gap: There is no pending/draft/submitted lifecycle: a partial save is indistinguishable from a submission, and because every slider defaults to 5 an evaluator can 'submit' an evaluation they never touched. The unscored-counts-as-0 fallback (pipeline.ts:377) further disagrees with the spec's blocking rule.
findings.fix: Add `evaluations.state` ∈ pending|draft|submitted (default pending). Split the workbench into Save draft (state=draft, no submitted_at) and Submit (state=submitted) with a server-side check that every applicable parameter — core 13 plus the caller's own additional params — has a value; leave sliders unset (null) until touched rather than defaulting to 5.

findings.title: Alignment call offers only 'Issue term sheet' — Renegotiate and Hold are missing
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/panel-alignmentcall.html — the last column 'Outcome' is a select with 'Issue term sheet', 'Renegotiate', 'Hold'; AISJ_VC_eval_roleflow_v2.png labels the Alignment call node "Issue term sheet · Renegotiate · Hold".
findings.repo: src/pipeline/vc.ts:132-138 — `alignment_call` has exactly one outgoing transition, `issue_term_sheet` → term_sheet. No renegotiate, no hold.
findings.gap: A deal at the alignment call can only move forward. There is no way to record a renegotiation loop or to park the deal, both of which the diagram and the panel specify.
findings.fix: Add `renegotiate` (alignment_call → alignment_call, or → partner_review if renegotiation reopens terms) and `hold` (alignment_call → alignment_call with a held flag) to vcPipeline, and surface both in the alignment call's action column.

findings.title: The PM's read-only-until-assigned sign-up gate is absent, and the PM has no sign-up nav item at all
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #83 — "a Program Manager's sign-up workspace is read-only until a Super User/Admin assigns them (pmAssigned)"; live-panels/AISJ_IC_PM_V5/_scripts.js:2034 `suwRO=!cuData[i].pmAssigned`, :2058 the amber read-only banner, :2102 the locked Sign-up pill
findings.repo: NONE for the gate — grep `pmAssigned` across src/ returns nothing. src/shared/nav.ts:78 `{ id: "incuration", label: "Sign up Pipeline", roles: ["admin", "program_associate"] }` — program_manager is not on the list, so the PM cannot reach the Sign up Pipeline at all (superuser bypasses via canSeeNav).
findings.gap: Two layers missing: the PM has no route to the sign-up surface, and even if they did there is no per-signup assignment flag to switch between the read-only and editable workspace.
findings.fix: Add program_manager to the `incuration` nav roles and add a per-signup PM assignment that gates the workspace read-only/editable.

findings.title: Capital deployment is reported but can never be recorded
findings.proto: Spec §8.3 step 3: "Capital deployment — record the deployment against the fund's committed capital (the 'Fund Deployment' surface that replaces the incubator's 'Seat capacity')"; §5 entity `Deck 1───0..1 CapitalDeployment`; §1 enum includes `deployed`.
findings.repo: src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:149 `INSERT INTO portfolio (id, deck_id, onboarded_at)` — capital_deployed is never supplied; the column is written only by the seed migrations/0008_seed_analytics.sql:103; src/server/routes/analytics.ts:205 reads `pf.capital_deployed` for the Capital Deployment & Pacing report. PARTIAL: the read path and the report screen exist, the write path does not.
findings.gap: The Capital screen renders numbers no user can enter or change, and the pipeline has no `deployed` stage between onboard_ready and portfolio.
findings.fix: Capture the deployment amount (and date) on the complete_legal_dd / onboard action, write it to portfolio.capital_deployed, and roll it up against programs.fund_size / fund_allocated so the pacing report is live.

findings.title: IC Member cannot score their 3 role parameters anywhere
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:2134 opens the report from panel-icpipeline with `{... role:'jury', roleName:'IC Member', customParams:[Barriers of entry, Scalability, Exit attractiveness], pcScored:true, icScored:true}`; :4399 the `icScored` branch renders an EDITABLE 'IC member — Addl. evaluation parameters … My score' table with an 'Average of my scores' row.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/VcEvaluatePage.tsx:19 `SCORING_STAGES = ["analyst_scoring","associate_review","partner_review"]`; src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:51 + :345 reject any score POST when the deal is not in those stages (409 not_in_scoring_stage); src/client/routes/IcVotePage.tsx:15 offers only the four ballot values. The parameters exist: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:61-71 (`vc_add_ic_1..3`, role_scope 'ic_member').
findings.gap: The IC lens is configured and stored but unreachable: no screen presents it and the server refuses the write. IC scores can never enter the report, so the §7 committee aggregation at the IC gate has nothing to aggregate.
findings.fix: Add `ic_review` to VC_SCORING_STAGES (server) and to the IC screen: render the IC member's three additional params as an editable block inside the IC Pipeline detail alongside the ballot, submitting via the existing POST /decks/:id/evaluate.

findings.title: The report is not stage-aware and not editable — none of the five stage flags exist
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:4229-4310 builds the core matrix per stage — analystScored → AI+analyst+2-way avg; introScored → AI+analyst+associate+3-way avg; partnerScored → AI+analyst+associate + an editable `<input type=number step=0.5>` 'My score' column with a per-parameter remarks textarea; pcScored → AI+analyst+associate+partner+4-way avg (read-only). :4392-4406 `custBlock` shows upstream roles via `roAddl(...)` marked 'Submitted / read-only' and the current role's block as editable. :4428 the `alignCall` branch adds an alignment-note textarea. :4434 the title flips between 'Evaluate' and 'Evaluation report'.
findings.repo: src/client/components/EvaluationReport.tsx — a read-only matrix with Core / Addl. tabs, no per-parameter expander, no average row, no inputs; src/server/routes/decks.ts:633-798 filters columns by role rank only (canSeeEvaluatorScores) with no notion of the stage the report was opened from. `grep -rn "pcScored|partnerScored|icScored|icRead|alignCall" src/` → 0 hits.
findings.gap: Section visibility is driven purely by who has already scored plus the viewer's rank, not by the gate. Nothing is editable in the report, so the prototype's core interaction — open the report at your gate, add your column inline, read upstream columns as reference — does not exist; scoring lives on a separate screen with a slider list.
findings.fix: Pass the opening stage into GET /decks/:id/report; return per-section `mode: editable|readonly|hidden` computed from the stage + the viewer's assignment, add the running N-way average column and an 'Average of scores' row per additional-parameter block, and let the current gate's column accept 0–10 (step 0.5) values and per-parameter remarks in place.

findings.title: The assignment confirm step has no instructions field, no notify toggle and no deadline, and cannot fan one deck out to several evaluators
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:1146 asConfirm() builds `rows` as the CROSS PRODUCT — `selectedDecks.forEach(d => members.forEach(mem => rows.push({…})))`. renderAs4() (:1159-1211) renders the summary card with rows "Decks", "Jury members", "Scope: N deck(s) × M jury member(s) = N×M evaluation(s)" and "Deadline: 7 days from assignment date", followed by an "Instructions to evaluators (optional)" textarea (placeholder "e.g. Focus on traction and team slide. Flag any ARR inconsistencies.") and a "Notify M jury members by email" toggle.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx:71-76 pairs deck i with `selectedMembers[i % selectedMembers.length]` — a round-robin SPREAD, and the UI says so at :326-327 ("{n} members (spread evenly)"); :106 `await assignDeck(deck.id, member.id)` one call per deck. The API body is `{ assigneeId }` only (src/server/routes/pipeline.ts:277) and the write is `UPDATE decks SET assigned_to = ?` (:298). `grep -rn "Instructions to evaluators|Notify|deadline" src/client/routes/AssignPage.tsx` returns nothing.
findings.gap: Distinct from the assignments-table finding, which is about persistence: even the semantics are inverted. The prototype assigns each selected deck to EVERY selected member (that is the point of "pick one or more jury members"); the repo divides the decks between them, so selecting 3 members for 3 decks produces 3 single-evaluator assignments instead of 9 evaluations. The optional evaluator instructions, the email-notify toggle and the 7-day deadline have no field, no column and no route parameter. This applies to the incubator Assign screen today and to whatever VC assign screen gets built.

findings.title: Branding & theme reduced from 18 token pickers to wordmark + tagline + one accent
