findings.repo: src/client/routes/ConfigPage.tsx:389-457 `BrandingSection` — Wordmark (one field), Tagline, one 'Accent colour' input, Live preview, Save. Persisted as free-form JSON in `org_settings.branding_json` (migrations/0001_init.sql:18; config.ts:348 PUT /api/config/branding). No `branding` slug in nav.ts
findings.gap: 16 of 18 colour tokens are not editable, the wordmark is one field instead of two, the logo image URL is gone, 'Reset to defaults' is gone, and edits do not apply live across the product because the repo palette is compiled Tailwind theme values rather than runtime-settable custom properties for the brand ramp.
findings.fix: Expose all 13 brand + 5 status tokens as :root custom properties, render the two picker cards, and add wordmark part 2 + logo URL + Reset.

findings.title: My Parameters lacks the weight select and the scoring description field
findings.proto: AISJ_IC_SuserV15/panel-myparams.html — per parameter: 'Parameter label', 'Scoring weight in their composite' select (Informational (not weighted) / 5% additional weight / 10% additional weight), 'Description shown to user during scoring' textarea, 'AI extraction prompt for this parameter' + 'Reset'; role tabs rt-pm / rt-pa / rt-men; toolbar 'Save all'. Spec §6.2 'Default weight Informational (not weighted into the composite unless the org raises it to 5% / 10%)'
findings.repo: src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx renders label + AI prompt only, with a fixed `<Badge tone="neutral">Informational · assistive</Badge>` (MyParamsPage.tsx:197) and owner roles stacked as cards rather than tabbed; server PUT /api/config/additional-params/:id accepts only `{name, prompt}` (config.ts:274-285); the `parameters` table has no `description` column (only 0013:18 added `prompt`)

Role tabs, 'Save all' and per-prompt 'Reset' are also absent.

findings.title: Role-parameter configuration is gated on the Premium plan; the prototype specifies Pro
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/panel-myparams.html, 'Role configurable parameters' card: 'Each role can add up to 3 custom evaluation parameters on top of the 13 standard areas. findings.repo: src/shared/plans.ts:33-35 `planAllowsAdditional(plan) { return PLAN_RANK[plan] >= PLAN_RANK.premium; }`. src/server/routes/config.ts:199-204 requirePremium and :221 gate every additional-param write on it. src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx:76-83 replaces the entire screen body with a lock EmptyState titled 'Additional parameters need a Premium plan' whenever cfg.additionalEnabled is false. findings.fix: Change planAllowsAdditional to `>= PLAN_RANK.pro` (matching planAllowsCore) and update the MyParamsPage lock copy, or confirm with the client which tier is authoritative — the prototype copy and the repo currently disagree.

findings.title: Stage ids do not match the spec's documented enum (repo follows the flow diagram instead)

findings.repo: src/pipeline/vc.ts:9-24 — uploaded, pending_ai, analyst_scoring, associate_review, partner_review, partner_call, investment_dd, ic_review, mp_decision, alignment_call, term_sheet, legal_dd, onboard_ready, archived.
findings.gap: Absent from the repo entirely: `sourced` (folded into uploaded), `intro` (intro calls hang off associate_review/partner_review with no stage of their own), `deployed`, `portfolio` (replaced by onboard_ready + a portfolio row) and `passed` (both pass and not-shortlisted land in `archived`, distinguished only by the derived Reason column in StagePage.tsx:434). findings.title: No credit ledger; orgs seeded on Premium instead of Standard + trial

But `grep -rn ledger src/ migrations/` finds no table; migrations/0002_seed.sql seeds `('incubator','premium',3)`; migrations/0007_config_plans_credits.sql:12 then sets `credits_balance = 50` for all; config.ts:99 GET /api/config/summary returns `creditsBalance` only

findings.title: No organizations or user_roles tables — `edition` doubles as the tenant, `role` is one column

findings.title: evaluations and evaluation_scores lack their spec'd columns

findings.title: No fund/vehicle thesis, target stage or ticket-size range — the data the Investment Associate's three canonical parameters are scored against

findings.title: No credit ledger and no trial-grant concept — only a running balance

findings.title: Deal-status enum diverges from the spec: no sourced, intro, diligence, deployed or portfolio states

findings.title: The evaluation report is not stage-aware: no ?stage= parameter, no editable/read-only/hidden role sections
findings.proto: live/specs/vc.html §8.4 (pcScored / partnerScored / icScored / icRead / alignCall) and §11 gotcha 5 — "the report reads which pipeline panel is visible and the stage flags"; §13 `GET /decks/:id/report?stage=intro|partner|ic|align`
findings.repo: src/server/routes/decks.ts:634 `decks.get("/:id/report", …)` reads no stage query param; src/client/api.ts:146 calls `/api/decks/${id}/report` bare; src/client/components/EvaluationReport.tsx:32 `type Tab = "core" | "additional"` — the only structure is two tabs

findings.title: The VC evaluation ladder contradicts the spec's own role mapping
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #vc-side-mapping-parallel-product-line-for-reference — "Managing Partner → Super User · Partner/Principal → Program Manager · IC Member → Jury Member · Investment Associate/Analyst → Program Associate"
findings.repo: src/shared/roles.ts:157-170 — incubator ranks program_associate 1, jury 2, program_manager 3; VC ranks analyst 1, associate 2, partner 3, ic_member 4.
findings.gap: Under the spec's mapping IC Member ≡ Jury Member and Partner ≡ Program Manager, so the VC ladder should place ic_member BELOW partner exactly as jury sits below program_manager. The repo inverts it, so the same logical role sees a different slice of the report depending on edition. It may be a deliberate call (the IC is the final decision body) — but it is a departure from the mapping the spec states, and it should be an explicit decision rather than a silent one.
findings.fix: Either derive the VC ranks from the §3 mapping, or record the deviation in the spec with the client's sign-off.

findings.title: The build was made against superseded prototype files
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #4-prototype-file-inventory — the canonical set is AISJ_IC_SuserV15.HTM · AISJ_IC_PM_V5.HTM · AISJ_IC_PA_V3.HTM · AISJ_IC_Jury_V4.html · AISJ_ICAdmin_V6.html · AISJ_LauncherV7.html
findings.repo: docs/FINISH-PLAN.md:147 cites `AISJ_INC_Jury_V3.html`; :164, :177, :366 cite `AISJ_IC_SuserV11.HTM`. FINISH-PLAN.md:366 records "The incubator prototype (AISJ_IC_SuserV11.HTM ~3308) only drew PM + Jury tabs (a blank 3rd)" — but live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/panel-myparams.html draws all three (rt-pm / rt-pa / rt-men).
findings.gap: The design of record moved two to four versions on and the build docs still point at the old files. This is the root cause of the §6.2 name divergence and of several §8.3 omissions — the older Superuser file did not carry the finished sign-up workspace.
findings.fix: Repoint docs/FINISH-PLAN.md at the V15/V5/V3/V4/V6 set and re-diff each screen against it before further work.

findings.title: Deck has no Ask, Valuation or DD fields the IC Pipeline table requires
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/panel-icpipeline.html — table headers Startup · Sector · Stage · AI score · Avg. score · Addl. parameters · DD · Ask · Valuation · Recommendation.
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql `decks` + all later ALTERs (0003, 0011, 0016, 0018, 0019, 0021) — no ask / raise / valuation / round column; src/client/routes/IcVotePage.tsx:107-200 renders a master-detail pane, not the ten-column table.
findings.gap: Three of the prototype's IC decision columns have no data model, so the committee decides without the round size, valuation or diligence status in front of it.
findings.fix: Add `decks.ask_amount`, `decks.valuation`, `decks.round` (AI-extractable from the deck) and derive a DD status from investment_dd; render the IC Pipeline as the specified ten-column table with the per-member recommendation select.

findings.title: A deck holds one storage key, not a DeckFile collection
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #5 — `Deck 1───∞ DeckFile (pitch deck upload)`; #12 `deck_files(deck_id, kind[pitch_deck|…], storage_url, uploaded_by, uploaded_at)`
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:66 `r2_key TEXT` on decks — a single column; migrations/0009_rescore_versioning.sql adds `deck_versions` for re-uploads but keeps the one-current-file shape. No deck_files table.
findings.gap: Only one file per deck, with no kind and no uploader attribution. The resubmit-deck loop overwrites rather than accumulating, and there is no place for the supporting documents a signup later needs.
findings.fix: Add deck_files with kind + uploaded_by; keep deck_versions as the version history over it.

findings.title: Clarifications are a per-round blob with no author and one answer
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #5 `Evaluation 1───0..1 IntroCallNote` context and #12 `founder_clarifications(id, deck_id, asked_by ⟶ users, question text, answer text, answered_at)`; #10 — "founders can respond to evaluator questions (round-trip Q&A tied to a deck)"
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:121-129 `queries(id, deck_id, questions TEXT, email_status, founder_response TEXT, created_at, resolved_at)` — `questions` is a single text blob, `founder_response` a single text blob, and there is no `asked_by`. No ALTER adds one (grep `ALTER TABLE queries` → zero hits).
findings.gap: Questions cannot be attributed to the evaluator who asked them, and a founder cannot answer question 2 without answering question 1 — they answer the round. The spec's per-question round-trip is flattened.
findings.fix: Normalise to one row per question with asked_by and its own answer/answered_at; keep the round as a grouping key for the outbound email.

findings.title: No Organization entity — the product is single-tenant, keyed by edition
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #5 — Organization is the root of five relationships (Program, User, ParameterDefinition, Subscription, SupportTicket); #12 `organizations(id, name, type[incubator|vc], canonical_domain, created_at)`
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:1-2 — "Single-tenant: one implicit organization; both editions (incubator | vc) coexist." `org_settings` (0001:19) is keyed by `edition`, not org id; no organizations table exists.
findings.gap: `edition` is doing double duty as both product line and tenant, so two incubator customers cannot coexist and the spec's per-organization configurability of the 13 areas (§1: "Treat the 13-area set and weights as per-organization configurable") is per-edition instead.
findings.fix: Confirm with the client whether multi-tenancy is in scope; if so, introduce organizations and re-key org_settings, parameters, programs, users and tickets on org_id.

findings.title: No Fund/Organization entity and no CreditLedgerEntry — settings are keyed by edition
findings.proto: Spec §5: `Fund(Organization) 1───∞ Vehicle(Program)`, `Fund 1───∞ User`, `Fund 1───∞ ParameterDefinition`, `Fund 1───1 Subscription 1───∞ CreditLedgerEntry`, `Fund 1───∞ SupportTicket`; §6.1 "Weights are per-fund configurable".
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql `org_settings` has `edition TEXT PRIMARY KEY` — exactly two rows, one per edition, holding plan + credits_balance + branding + thresholds; there is no funds/orgs table (full CREATE TABLE inventory: call_participants, calls, cohorts, deck_extractions, deck_onboarding, deck_versions, decks, email_outbox, evaluations, ic_votes, investment_dd, legal_dd, messages, org_settings, parameters, pipeline_events, portfolio, programs, queries, resubmit_tokens, rubric_anchors, scores, sectors, term_sheets, tickets, users). Credits are a bare integer with no ledger.
findings.gap: The build is single-tenant per edition: two funds cannot hold different weights, plans, branding or credit balances, and credit movements leave no audit trail even though §10 meters one credit per deck evaluated.
findings.fix: Introduce `funds(id, edition, …)`, re-key org_settings/parameters/users/programs on fund_id, and add `credit_ledger(fund_id, delta, reason, deck_id, actor_id, created_at)` with the balance derived from it.

findings.title: Core weights are not validated to sum to 100%
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #61 — "Weights sum to 100% and feed the AI/human composite"; #1 table sums to exactly 100
findings.repo: src/server/routes/config.ts:171-175 validates each weight in 0..100 individually and then batches the updates; no sum check anywhere in the handler (config.ts:151-190).
findings.gap: An admin can save weights totalling 60 or 140. The composite still normalises by Σweight so it stays 0–10, but the "Weight" column in the report (EvaluationReport.tsx:93 renders `{row.weight}%`) then prints percentages that do not add to 100.
findings.fix: Reject a PUT whose core weights do not total 100, and surface the running total in the Area weights editor.

findings.title: Core areas share one global AI prompt instead of a per-area extraction prompt
findings.proto: Spec §6.1: "Each area is scored 0–10, has a five-band rubric (§7), an AI-extraction prompt, and a weight defined in-file." live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:440-442 — each of the 13 areas carries its own `prompt:'Does the problem matter, and to whom? Evaluate against the rubric anchors below…'` plus five `criteria` clarification questions.
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:19 adds `parameters.prompt` but seeds it NULL for core areas ("NULL for core areas, which fall back to name + weight"); src/server/routes/config.ts:177 `UPDATE parameters SET weight = ?, name = ?` — the core PUT cannot set a prompt; src/client/routes/ConfigPage.tsx:331-375 exposes one org-wide `ai_system_prompt`.
findings.gap: The 13 per-area prompts and their 5 clarification questions each have no storage or editor, so the AI scores all 13 areas from names and weights alone and the Query screen has no per-area question bank to draw on.
findings.fix: Populate `parameters.prompt` for the 13 core rows from the prototype's `params()` seed, expose it in the Core Parameters editor, and add a `parameter_questions` table seeded from each area's `criteria` for the Query flow.

findings.title: Pipeline ranking blends the AI composite into the jury average
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #7 — "Jury aggregation: across all jury evaluations of a deck, average the per-parameter scores (and the composite). This average is what ranks the pipeline."; #12 `deck_jury_score = avg of jury evaluations.composite`, `deck_pipeline_rank = order by deck_jury_score`
findings.repo: src/shared/scoring.ts:56-64 `decisionScore` = `(ai + mean(humanTotals)) / 2`, and with no human evaluation it returns the AI composite alone.
findings.gap: The number that drives the shortlist decision (and the per-program shortlist floor) is half AI, where the spec ranks on the jury average. A deck with a high AI score and a weak jury verdict ranks above one the jury preferred.
findings.fix: Rank on the jury average; keep the AI composite as a separate displayed column, and decide explicitly (with the client) what an unscored deck ranks as.

findings.title: Score input is whole-number, not the specified 0.5 step
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #7 — "Per-area score: integer/half-step 0–10 (step 0.5)"
findings.repo: src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:245-248 `<input type="range" min={0} max={10} step={1} …>`
findings.gap: An evaluator cannot record a 7.5. The AI path and the aggregation already carry decimals (weightedTotal rounds to 2dp), so this is a UI-only restriction that silently coarsens human scores relative to AI ones.
findings.fix: Set step to 0.5 on the human score input and format the value to one decimal.

findings.title: Zero-weight composite returns 0 instead of falling back to the AI value
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #7 — "composite = Σ(score_i × weight_i) / Σ(weight_i); if no weights, fall back to the raw AI value"
findings.repo: src/shared/scoring.ts:13-14 `if (totalWeight === 0) return 0;`
findings.gap: An org that zeroes every core weight (reachable — config.ts:172 permits weight 0 on every parameter and never checks the sum) gets a composite of 0 for every deck rather than the AI value, which reads as "all decks scored zero" rather than "unweighted".
findings.fix: Pass the AI composite into weightedTotal as the zero-weight fallback.

findings.title: Score step is 1, not the specified 0.5
findings.proto: Spec §7: "Per-area score: integer/half-step 0–10 (step 0.5)". live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_scripts.js:4287 `<input class="jr-myin" type="number" min="0" max="10" step="0.5" …>`; :4847 `vcAddlScore` rounds to the nearest 0.5.
findings.repo: src/client/components/EvalScorecard.tsx:248 and :306 `step={1}` on both the core and the additional-parameter range inputs.
findings.gap: Half-step scores cannot be entered, so the repo cannot represent the granularity the whole prototype displays (every score chip renders one decimal).
findings.fix: Set step={0.5} on both inputs; the server already clamps to 0–10 without rounding.

findings.title: VC call tables label the human-score column 'Jury score' instead of 'Partner'
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/panel-partnercall.html and panel-alignmentcall.html — columns Startup · AI score · Partner · Avg. score · Addl. Parameter scores · Call scheduled · Call date · Call completed · Schedule call · Sponsorship|Outcome.
findings.repo: src/client/routes/CallsPage.tsx:419 `<th …>Jury score</th>` hard-coded for both editions; the CallsConfig doc-comment at :61-62 promises "Column header for the human-score column (Jury vs Analyst per edition)" but no such field exists on the interface (:54-69).
findings.gap: A VC partner sees an incubator word on their own call screen; the config field that was meant to fix this was never added. The prototype's Sponsorship / Outcome column header also differs per screen (repo says 'Actions' on both).
findings.fix: Add `humanScoreLabel` and `actionLabel` to CallsConfig and set them per screen ('Partner' + 'Sponsorship' / 'Outcome' on VC, 'Jury score' on incubator).

findings.title: The evaluation report is not stage-aware, and its hierarchy filter contradicts the spec
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #84-assignment-report-stage-awareness; live-panels/AISJ_IC_Jury_V4/_scripts.js:3394-3400 `function stage()` detects the visible panel and 3374-3375 documents "Assigned → Program associate parameters (reference); Intro calls → Program associate + Program manager parameters"
findings.repo: src/server/routes/decks.ts:633-634 `decks.get("/:id/report")` reads no stage/query param; src/client/api.ts:145 `getDeckReport(id)` passes none. src/server/routes/decks.ts:719-721 filters columns by `canSeeEvaluatorScores(edition, role, evaluatorRole)`, where src/shared/roles.ts:157-162 ranks jury=2 below program_manager=3.
findings.gap: Two failures. (a) No stage parameter exists, so the report cannot show PA+PM at the Assign stage or PA+PM+Jury at Intro calls. (b) The rank filter actively forbids what §8.4 requires: a jury member is denied the Program Manager column, yet the Jury prototype renders exactly that reference section on Intro calls. A program associate (rank 1) is likewise denied the PM section the spec grants at the Assign stage.
findings.fix: Add `?stage=` to the report route and let stage-driven reference sections override the rank filter where §8.4 names them.

findings.title: Role-parameter names diverge from the canonical §6.2 set
findings.proto: spec §6.2 'Consistency rule: these role-parameter names are canonical across every file' — PM: TRL stage, Product-Market Fit, Traction; PA: Program fit, Investment stage, Ask; Jury: Barriers of entry, Scalability, Industry growth. AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js `ROLE_PARAMS = {pm:[TRL stage, Product-Market Fit, Traction], pa:[Program fit, Investment stage, Ask], jury:[Barriers of entry, Scalability, Industry growth]}`; panel-myparams.html shows the same. §11 explicitly flags the old placeholder names as the thing to align
findings.repo: migrations/0013_role_additional_params.sql:24-47 seeds Program & Mandate Fit / Application Readiness / Founder Coachability Signal (PA), Program Fit / Mentor Engagement Potential / Cohort Contribution Potential (PM), Founder Resilience & Coachability / Product-Market Fit Signal / Team Execution Capability (jury)
findings.gap: All nine incubator role parameters carry the superseded placeholder names, and their descriptions/prompts differ from the spec's. These names surface in My Parameters, the Evaluate form, the report and every role-attributed analytic.
findings.fix: Reseed the nine parameters with the §6.2 names, descriptions and AI prompts.

findings.title: My account, Buy credits and Issue log appear where the prototype has no such item
findings.proto: AISJ_IC_PM_V5, AISJ_IC_PA_V3, AISJ_IC_Jury_V4 _sidebar.html carry no 'My account'; no role file's sidebar carries 'Buy credits' or 'Issue log'; AISJ_ICAdmin_V6/_sidebar.html has no Collaborate group (no Contact Admin / Contact team)
findings.repo: src/shared/nav.ts:109 `account` for admin+PM+PA+jury; nav.ts:111 `billing` 'Buy credits'; nav.ts:119 `issues` 'Issue log' for all internal roles; nav.ts:113-114 contactadmin/contactteam include admin
findings.gap: Three extra sidebar items for roles the prototype does not give them, plus a Collaborate group on the Admin role. Issue log is a sanctioned repo addition (FINISH-PLAN §4/S7); My account and Buy credits are not accounted for.
findings.fix: Trim account to the roles whose prototype sidebar shows it, or record the deliberate deviation.

findings.title: Five pipeline panels render from the generic StagePage config
findings.proto: AISJ_IC_SuserV15 panel-jurypipeline.html, panel-forsignup.html, panel-incuration.html, panel-curation.html, panel-archive.html are bespoke screens
findings.repo: src/client/App.tsx:111-112 `const stage = INCUBATOR_STAGE_CONFIG[navId]; if (stage) return <StagePage config={stage} />`; StagePage.tsx:669-758 defines jurypipeline, pmpipeline, incuration, curation, archive as five column/action configs on one table component
findings.gap: Five of the 22 canonical panels are one shared table shape driven by config, not the prototype's per-screen layouts. Flagged here at inventory level; the per-screen column/action/KPI diffs belong to the panel lanes.
findings.fix: Keep StagePage as the base but restore each screen's own toolbar, KPI tiles and column set.

findings.title: Tagline capitalisation differs
findings.proto: spec §14 Tagline: 'Venture Intelligence First.'; panel-branding.html live preview 'Venture Intelligence First'
findings.repo: src/client/routes/LoginPage.tsx:49 'Venture intelligence first.' (ConfigPage.tsx:391 uses the correct 'Venture Intelligence First' as the branding default)
findings.gap: The login screen renders the tagline in sentence case; the branding default is title case. Two spellings in one product.

findings.title: Top bar shows the edition label instead of the tagline; login copy is cased differently
findings.proto:
AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_topnav.html — `
Venture Intelligence First
` sits directly under the wordmark; live/specs/vc.html §14 Tagline: "Venture Intelligence First."
findings.repo: src/client/components/Topbar.tsx:48-64 renders `<Logo size={26} />` then `editionLabel`; src/client/routes/LoginPage.tsx:49 "Venture intelligence first."

findings.title: Role identifiers and the Admin label differ from the spec
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #12 role enum `super_user | program_manager | program_associate | jury_member | admin`; #3 names the role "Admin (Client Admin)"; panel-myparams.html's "Previewing as" list reads "Client Admin"
findings.repo: src/shared/roles.ts:9-16 `superuser`, `jury` (not `super_user`, `jury_member`); src/shared/roles.ts:55 `admin: "Admin"`.
findings.gap: Two identifier spellings differ from the spec's enum, and the user-facing Admin label drops the "Client Admin" qualifier the prototype shows. Cosmetic on its own, but the identifiers leak into the API surface (§13's `?scope=pm|pa|jury|standard` vs the repo's role_scope values) and into any client-supplied data import.
findings.fix: Either align the identifiers to the spec enum or record the mapping explicitly; set the Admin label to "Client Admin" where the prototype does.

findings.title: Two VC role labels differ from the prototype chrome
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_VC_Partner_V1/_topnav.html shows 'Ishaan Sethi · Partner/Principal'; live-panels/AISJ_VC_Admin_V4/_topnav.html shows 'Nisha Kapoor · Administrator'; AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/_topnav.html shows both 'Managing Partner' (title) and 'Super User' (role).
findings.repo: src/shared/roles.ts:60-67 — vc labels are 'Managing Partner', 'Admin', 'Partner', 'IC Member', 'Investment Associate', 'Analyst'.
findings.gap: 'Partner' vs 'Partner / Principal' and 'Admin' vs 'Administrator'. The superuser case is also collapsed: the prototype shows the title and the role separately, the repo shows only 'Managing Partner'.
findings.fix: Set partner → 'Partner / Principal' and admin → 'Administrator' in ROLE_LABELS.vc; render the superuser chip as title + role where the topbar has room.

findings.title: Restore excludes the associate, who is allowed to archive
findings.proto: AISJ_VC_eval_roleflow_v2.png — 'Not shortlisted · Archived, revivable', reached by dashed edges from BOTH the Associate and the Partner nodes.
findings.repo: src/pipeline/vc.ts:57-63 `not_shortlisted` roles include `associate`; :155-161 `restore` roles are `["partner","admin","superuser"]` — the associate is absent.
findings.gap: An associate can archive a deal but cannot undo it, which makes their own mistake unrecoverable without escalating.
findings.fix: Add `associate` to the restore transition's roles.

findings.title: The `uploaded` stage and `submit_for_ai` transition are dead code
findings.proto: AISJ_VC_eval_roleflow_v2.png — the Analyst node covers "Upload · AI eval · core scores" as one intake step.
findings.repo: src/pipeline/vc.ts:8 `initialStage: "uploaded"` and :36-42 the `submit_for_ai` transition; but src/server/routes/decks.ts:1009 inserts every new deck directly at `'pending_ai'`, so nothing ever occupies `uploaded`.
findings.gap: A stage and a transition exist that no deck can reach, and `initialStage` misdescribes the real entry point. Harmless today, misleading to anyone reading the machine as documentation.
findings.fix: Either drop `uploaded` and set initialStage to `pending_ai`, or have storeDeck insert at `uploaded` and fire submit_for_ai so the audit trail records the intake step.

findings.title: Spec calls archived terminal; the prototype and repo both allow Restore
findings.proto: live/specs/incubator.html #82 — "archived and rejected are terminal"; but live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/_scripts.js:1791 `lifecycleOpts` offers `['restore','Restore']` and :1796 `if (val === 'restore'){ d.signup = 'shortlisted'; }`, and panel-archive.html's subtitle reads "Restore any of them back into the workflow."
findings.repo: src/pipeline/incubator.ts:27-29 marks archived non-terminal with the comment "Aug-2026 issue 31: Archive offers 'Restore back into the workflow'", and :140-157 defines `restore` out of both rejected and archived.
findings.gap: The spec sentence is stale relative to its own prototype and to the Aug-2026 issue log. The repo is correct here — flagging so the spec is corrected rather than the code.
findings.fix: Amend §8.2 to say archived/rejected are terminal except for the explicit Restore action; note that the repo restores to `ai_evaluated` while the prototype restores to `shortlisted` — pick one.

findings.title: Sidebar 'All decks' count pill missing

findings.repo: src/client/components/Sidebar.tsx — no count or badge rendering (`grep -n 'badge|count' Sidebar.tsx` matches only a comment on line 31)
findings.gap: No live deck count on the primary nav item.
findings.fix: Render a count pill on alldecks fed by the deck list query.

findings.title: No per-parameter description field exists anywhere, and Program Managers cannot edit their own parameters despite the prototype granting it by default
findings.proto: live-panels/AISJ_IC_SuserV15/panel-myparams.html — every one of the nine parameters carries THREE authored fields: 'Parameter label', 'Description shown to user during scoring' (e.g. TRL stage: 'Rate the maturity of the startup's technology on the Technology Readiness Level scale (1–9)…') and 'AI extraction prompt', plus a Reset control per prompt, a 'Save all parameters' and a 'Preview in scoring view' button. The header states the permission rule verbatim: 'Super Users, Program Managers and Client Admins can edit by default. Other roles are read-only here unless granted the "Configure 3 additional parameters" permission in Admin → Team & roles.', backed by a 'Previewing as' switcher (Super User / Client Admin / Program Manager / Program Associate / Jury Member) that flips a 'Permission granted' pill and a read-only banner. Identical in AISJ_VC_Superuser_V8/panel-myparams.html and in the old snapshot, so this is standing spec, not drift.
findings.repo: migrations/0001_init.sql:30-40 parameters(id, edition, key, name, weight, informational, role_scope, sort_order, active) + migrations/0013 ALTER TABLE parameters ADD COLUMN prompt — there is no description/help column, and src/client/routes/MyParamsPage.tsx only ever edits name and prompt (ParamRow renders exactly two fields). MyParamsPage.tsx:31 `const canEdit = user?.role === "admin" || user?.role === "superuser";` so a program_manager falls into the read-only branch ('ask a Super User or Admin to configure these parameters'). No preview-as switcher, no per-prompt Reset, no 'Preview in scoring view'. (Note: the per-parameter 5%/10% weight select is deliberately not implemented per docs/FINISH-PLAN.md:404-406, so that one is excluded here.)
findings.gap: Two independent misses. (1) The description the evaluator is meant to read while scoring — authored for all nine parameters in both editions of the live set — has no column, no API field and no UI, so the guidance never reaches the scoring view. (2) The role that the prototype says can edit by default, the Program Manager, is locked out; and because there is no permission model (see the Team & roles finding), the 'Configure 3 additional parameters' grant that would open it up to others cannot exist either.
findings.fix: Add parameters.description (surfaced in EvalScorecard next to each additional param) and widen canEdit to program_manager/admin/superuser, ideally sourced from a permission record rather than a hard-coded role list.

findings.title: The whole Cohort summary report is computed on the AI pre-score, but the prototype's numbers are the FINAL post-juror scores

The KPI 'Avg weighted score / 10 = 6.4' and the 5-band 'Score distribution' therefore also read on final scores.
findings.repo: src/server/routes/analytics.ts:90-125 (/cohort selects `id, name, sector, stage, status, ai_score FROM decks` and never calls humanEvalsByDeck, unlike /drift:162 and /scoring:181); src/shared/analytics.ts:177-222 cohortSummary filters `d.aiScore !== null`, ranks by aiScore, averages aiScore and bands aiScore; src/client/routes/analytics/IncubatorReports.tsx:53 caption openly says "Weighted AI scores across every uploaded deck"
findings.gap: Every headline number on the Cohort summary — avg score, the 5-band distribution, and the 'Top of cohort — weighted ranking' table — is the AI pre-score, so a deck the jury moved from 6.4 to 7.6 is still ranked and banded at 6.4. The prototype's own cross-panel arithmetic proves this report is meant to be the post-review view; the repo's is a pre-review view wearing the same title. Human evaluation totals are already joined for two other reports in the same file.
findings.fix: Join mean human weighted_total per deck in the /cohort handler (reuse humanEvalsByDeck), pass it into cohortSummary, and score/rank/band on the final score with the AI score as fallback when no human evaluation exists.

Nothing grants a trial on account creation, nothing labels the first three decks as free, and nothing distinguishes trial credits from purchased ones — so the four prototype surfaces that advertise it, and the Upload sub-line that reports it, have no data to render. The auditor counted the acs-plan trial strip as one missing block inside finding #13, but not the absence of the underlying concept.
findings.fix: Add a trial grant to the account/org record (e.g. trial_credits_granted + granted_at on org_settings, or a credit_grants table distinguishing trial from purchased), surface it in the config summary, and render the strip on the account/plan/payment/success screens plus the Upload sub-line. findings.fix: Make the EmptyState role-aware in SetupWizard.tsx TeamStep: for admin/superuser keep the text and add an actual `<Link to="/app/admin">` (it is currently unlinked prose); for the read-only and cohorts seats, say instead that adding team members is a Super User / Admin action and name who to ask. findings.title: /api/messages has no founder or mentor gate — the internal team channel is readable by external founders
findings.proto: Contact team / Contact Admin are internal-only screens: they exist only in the 10 staff role files (panel-contactteam.html) and the founder has no such panel — the founder prototype is the isolated portal overlay `#fp-ov` / `fp-*` in _rest.html, which contains no Collaborate screen. The repo encodes the same intent at src/shared/nav.ts:120-124 + 203-205 ('Founder portal (isolated)').
findings.repo: src/server/routes/support.ts:253-254 — `const messages = new Hono<AppEnv>(); messages.use("*", requireAuth);` (no denyMentor, no denyFounder), contrast :103 `issues.use("*", requireAuth, denyMentor)` + :106-108 denyFounder; support.ts:62 POST /api/tickets is likewise bare requireAuth. scripts/role-matrix.ts:423-475 has probes for tickets.list / issues.list / issues.file / issues.triage but NO probe for /api/messages at all.
findings.gap: Founders hold real sessions (the repo says so itself at support.ts:101-107: 'founders … legitimately hold a session for the portal'), and the mentor user-type does too. Because the messages router applies only requireAuth, a founder or mentor can call GET /api/messages?scope=team and read the entire internal Collaborate channel — every message any staff member broadcast in that edition — and POST into it, and can also POST /api/tickets into the Admin queue. The client route guard (guards.tsx:29-44) hides the screen but the API is directly reachable, and the repo's stated model is that 'the API enforces authZ independently'. The role harness has no probe for these endpoints, so nothing catches it. This is the same class of defect as the mentor-authorization fixes already applied elsewhere via denyMentor.
findings.fix: Add `denyMentor` to the messages router and a denyFounder check on both messages handlers (and denyMentor on POST /api/tickets), then add messages.read / messages.send probes to scripts/role-matrix.ts so the matrix covers them.
